positive:0.en: Inside the map room of Silverfang's ship, dusty charts covered every wall. Old Helm spread a new piece of sky-paper on the table and studied it closely. 'This route leads straight to the Crystal Shelf,' he said, his voice *positive* and calm. Bell leaned in, eyes wide with hope.
positive:0.cnHint: 老舵在地图室里____地确认新航线，小铃满眼期待。
positive:0.hook: But one corner of the map had already begun to burn.
positive:0.line: 'I am *positive* this route will take us there safely.'

economic:0.en: Silverfang's trading post sat at the centre of the floating island, loud and busy. Crates of rare sky-fruit were stacked high. Old Helm whispered that the whole island ran on a single *economic* rule: every word you learn buys you one hour of shelter. Bell pulled out her notebook at once.
economic:0.cnHint: 银牙的岛上有一条奇特的____规则，小铃立刻掏出笔记本。
economic:0.hook: Someone had already crossed out the rule on the public board.
economic:0.line: 'The *economic* rule here is simple — learn or leave.'

link:0.en: In the lower cabin, Bell found a wall covered in thin silver chains. Each chain was a *link* between two floating islands on the old map, showing which places shared the same sky-wind. She traced one chain with her finger and gasped. It led straight to an island no one in the troupe had ever named.
link:0.cnHint: 小铃在船舱里发现银链是两座岛屿之间的____，顺着一条链她倒吸一口气。
link:0.hook: The chain at the far end was still warm to the touch.
link:0.line: 'Every *link* in this chain marks a path only the wind remembers.'

produce:0.en: Old Helm stood at the small stove in the galley, stirring a pot of glowing soup. He claimed that certain words, spoken aloud over heat, could *produce* a bright mist that shows hidden doors. Bell said nothing, but she quietly repeated the word he had just taught her, watching the steam curl upward.
produce:0.cnHint: 老舵说念出特定词语能____一种神秘雾气，小铃悄悄跟着念。
produce:0.hook: A thin door appeared in the wall where there had been only wood.
produce:0.line: 'Say it clearly — the right word will *produce* the light we need.'

teach:0.en: Silverfang sat across from Bell at a round iron table, a cup of warm sky-tea between them. He tapped a word card and slid it toward her. 'Let me *teach* you the traders' tongue,' he said with a rare smile. Outside, the wind picked up, as if the island itself was listening.
teach:0.cnHint: 银牙在圆桌旁主动要____小铃商人们的语言，窗外风声骤起。
teach:0.hook: The word on the card was one Bell had seen on a locked door.
teach:0.line: 'Sit down — I will *teach* you what that word truly means.'

worth:0.en: The troupe gathered around a small chest Old Helm had found behind a shelf. Inside lay a single gold word-tile. Silverfang studied it and said only three islands in the whole sky were *worth* trading for such a tile. The room went quiet. Everyone knew that meant a very long journey ahead.
worth:0.cnHint: 老舵发现的金色词牌只有三座岛____去换，室内一片寂静。
worth:0.hook: Silverfang then named only two of the three islands.
worth:0.line: 'That tile is *worth* more than any map we have ever carried.'

common:0.en: Bell asked why every island in the region used the same greeting word. Old Helm laughed and said some words become *common* the way rivers share the same rain — no one chooses it, it simply happens. Silverfang looked less amused. He folded his arms and stared at the ceiling as if hiding something.
common:0.cnHint: 老舵解释为何某些词会变得____，银牙却若有所思地望着天花板。
common:0.hook: Silverfang then quietly removed one word card from the board.
common:0.line: 'A *common* word is not a simple word — remember that.'

daily:0.en: Every morning on the ship, Bell noticed the same small ceremony: Old Helm wrote one new word on a strip of paper and pinned it above the porthole. He called it his *daily* offering to the sky. Bell started her own strip that very day, and the window seemed to let in a little more light.
daily:0.cnHint: 老舵每天都有一个____仪式——把新词贴在舷窗上，小铃也开始效仿。
daily:0.hook: That evening, both strips fluttered though the window was shut.
daily:0.line: 'One word a day — that is my *daily* gift to the journey.'

policy:0.en: Inside the map-room, Silverfang slapped a rolled chart on the table. 'Our *policy* is simple,' he said, eyeing Old Helm across the lantern light. 'First crew to name the island claims the word.' Old Helm smiled and set down a steaming cup. I held my breath, already learning that every rule here carried the smell of adventure.
policy:0.cnHint: 银牙在地图室里宣布了一条关于岛屿命名权的____，老舵与他对视而笑。
policy:0.hook: Old Helm's smile hid something Silverfang had not yet read.
policy:0.line: 'Our *policy* is simple: first crew to name the island wins the word.'

industry:0.en: The lower deck of the airship buzzed with quiet *industry*: Bell sketched charts, Old Helm stitched a torn sail, and Silverfang sharpened a compass needle with steady focus. I watched them all and understood — every floating island we sought had been earned, not given. I picked up a pen and started my own map.
industry:0.cnHint: 船舱里一片忙碌的____景象，每个人都在为下一座岛屿做准备。
industry:0.hook: The compass needle caught the starlight and pointed somewhere new.
industry:0.line: 'All this *industry* tonight means we reach the next island by dawn.'

concern:0.en: Bell frowned at the navigation glass, and her *concern* filled the small cabin like fog. 'The star-path is shifting,' she said softly. Old Helm crossed the room in two steps and looked. Silverfang leaned in from the doorway. Even I felt the weight of it — a moving sky meant a moving map, and our next word was already drifting.
concern:0.cnHint: 贝尔对星路的变化表示出深深的____，整个船舱的气氛随之凝固。
concern:0.hook: Somewhere beneath us, the next island was already drifting away.
concern:0.line: 'My *concern* is that the star-path has shifted since last night.'

present:0.en: Old Helm set a small carved box on the table and pushed it toward me. 'A *present*,' he said, 'for your first week with the troupe.' Inside lay a blank word-card, edges trimmed in gold. Bell clapped once. Silverfang only shrugged, but I caught the corner of a smile. I ran my thumb along the gold edge and felt ready for anything.
present:0.cnHint: 老舵送给我一个____，那是一张镶金边的空白词卡，象征着新的旅程。
present:0.hook: A blank card, I realized, was an island no one had named yet.
present:0.line: 'Think of it as a *present* for surviving your first week with us.'

claim:0.en: Silverfang pressed a finger on the chart and looked around the lantern-lit table. 'I *claim* the northern route,' he said, voice low and certain. Bell raised an eyebrow. Old Helm only poured more tea. I watched the silence stretch like open sky, learning that on this troupe, every choice was a kind of flag planted in the unknown.
claim:0.cnHint: 银牙在地图旁郑重地____了北方航线的优先权，众人陷入沉默。
claim:0.hook: Bell's raised eyebrow meant the northern route hid something unsaid.
claim:0.line: 'I *claim* the northern route — and I'll prove it's the shorter one.'

half:0.en: Bell divided the star-chart down the middle with her finger. 'We each take *half*,' she said, sliding one side toward Silverfang without looking at him. 'First to decode their portion finds the next island.' Silverfang stared at the paper, then at Bell, and for once said nothing. I leaned in, heart quick, hoping Old Helm would hand me a corner of my own.
half:0.cnHint: 贝尔把星图一分为二，提议各拿____，看谁先解读出新岛屿的位置。
half:0.hook: Silverfang stared at his half as if it already held a secret he feared.
half:0.line: 'Take *half* the chart and we will see whose reading proves right.'

successful:0.en: Old Helm pinned the new word-card to the board and turned to face us, satisfied. 'Every *successful* crossing starts the same way,' he said, 'with someone willing to look foolish for five minutes.' Bell laughed. Silverfang crossed his arms but nodded slowly. I wrote the words down, feeling that the lesson was worth more than any single island we might reach.
successful:0.cnHint: 老舵贴上新词卡，说每一次____的穿越都始于某人愿意短暂显得愚蠢。
successful:0.hook: Silverfang's slow nod told me even rivals kept Old Helm's lessons close.
successful:0.line: 'Every *successful* voyage began with someone willing to look foolish first.'

access:0.en: The archive door was old iron, marked with faded word-signs. 'Only the troupe leader has *access*,' Bell told me, standing close and keeping her voice low. Then Old Helm pressed a single word-card to the lock, the door sighed open, and warm golden light spilled out. He waved us all inside. Silverfang went first, which surprised no one.
access:0.cnHint: 档案室的铁门只有团长凭词卡才能____，里面透出温暖的金色光芒。
access:0.hook: The golden light inside promised maps of islands no one had named yet.
access:0.line: 'Only the troupe leader has *access*, but tonight Old Helm opened it for all of us.'

determine:0.en: Inside Silverfang's cabin, maps covered every wall. Old Helm studied the oldest one, tracing its torn edge with a careful finger. 'We must *determine* which island matches this shape before dawn,' he said quietly, 'or the bet is already lost.' The candle burned low between us.
determine:0.cnHint: 老船长仔细研究地图，试图____哪座岛屿与残图吻合。
determine:0.hook: The torn edge matched something none of us expected.
determine:0.line: 'We must *determine* the answer before the candle dies.'

response:0.en: Silverfang crossed her arms and waited. Old Helm had challenged her claim about the northern route, and the whole troupe fell silent. Her *response* came slowly — a single folded chart dropped onto the table. It showed a path none of us had ever seen, and it proved him wrong.
response:0.cnHint: 银牙用一张地图作为____，回应了老舵手的质疑。
response:0.hook: That chart should not have existed at all.
response:0.line: 'My *response* to your doubt is right here on this table.'

search:0.en: Bell knelt beside the heavy chest and lifted out bundle after bundle of old notes. Her *search* for the missing island token had already taken an hour. Silverfang leaned in the doorway, watching with half-closed eyes, saying nothing. Outside, the wind pushed at the cabin walls and the stars shifted.
search:0.cnHint: 贝尔在箱子里____那枚失落的岛屿令牌，已经找了整整一个小时。
search:0.hook: Then Bell's hand went still inside the chest.
search:0.line: 'This *search* is taking too long — let me help you.'

due:0.en: Old Helm placed three sky-coins on the table, calm as ever. 'These are *due* to Silverfang if her route proves correct by morning,' he announced. No one argued. Bell quietly recorded the amount in her log. I watched the coins shine in the candlelight, wondering which side of the bet would win.
due:0.cnHint: 老舵手宣布，如果银牙的航路被证实，这些硬币将____归还给她。
due:0.hook: Morning was only four short hours away.
due:0.line: 'The coins are *due* to her the moment we confirm the route.'

regard:0.en: I had always heard sailors *regard* Silverfang as the finest navigator on the floating islands. Seeing her now, bent over charts and speaking in quick, sharp sentences, I understood why. Old Helm listened without interrupting — a rare thing for him. Even Bell set down her pen to pay attention.
regard:0.cnHint: 水手们都____银牙为浮岛上最出色的领航者。
regard:0.hook: But tonight, even she looked uncertain.
regard:0.line: 'We *regard* her as the best — and tonight she must prove it.'

true:0.en: 'Tell me something *true*,' Silverfang said, pressing one finger to the centre of the map. Bell looked up from her notes, surprised. Old Helm folded his hands. 'That island,' he said softly, 'is exactly where your chart says it is.' A small silence followed, warm and full of something like relief.
true:0.cnHint: 银牙要求大家说一句____的话，老舵手的回答让船舱里安静了片刻。
true:0.hook: Relief did not last long in a cabin full of rivals.
true:0.line: 'Tell me something *true* about that island's location.'

depend:0.en: Silverfang spread both hands flat on the table. 'Everything we do next will *depend* on whether this reading is correct,' she said, tapping the tiny number scrawled in the map's corner. Bell checked it twice. Old Helm nodded once, slowly. Outside, I heard the anchor chain shift and groan in the wind.
depend:0.cnHint: 银牙说，下一步怎么走将完全____这个数字是否正确。
depend:0.hook: The number had been written by someone long dead.
depend:0.line: 'Our next move will *depend* entirely on Bell's calculation.'

expensive:0.en: The token Silverfang placed on the table was small but beautiful — pale blue glass set in copper wire. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. 'That looks *expensive*,' he said. 'It is,' she replied without smiling. 'Which is why losing this bet would hurt.' Bell and I exchanged a careful glance across the candlelight.
expensive:0.cnHint: 银牙押上了一枚____的令牌，老舵手看到后挑起了眉毛。
expensive:0.hook: Nobody in the room wanted to be the one to lose it.
expensive:0.line: 'That token is *expensive* — are you sure you want to bet it?'

explain:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm unrolled a strange chart covered in symbols none of us could read. He pointed at a glowing mark near the centre and began to *explain* how each symbol matched a floating island we had not yet visited. I listened closely, feeling the room grow warmer with possibility.
explain:0.cnHint: 老船长在地图室里向大家____那些神秘符号的含义。
explain:0.hook: But one symbol had no island to match it.
explain:0.line: 'Let me *explain* why this mark should frighten us all.'

examine:0.en: Bell spread the recovered word-fragment across the low table and leaned in close. She asked for the lantern, then began to *examine* every edge and corner, her fingers tracing lines too faint for the rest of us to see. Old Helm stood at the door, arms folded, waiting in silence.
examine:0.cnHint: 小铃仔细____那块刚找回的词语碎片，试图发现隐藏的线索。
examine:0.hook: Her breath stopped at the fragment's hidden edge.
examine:0.line: '*Examine* it carefully — one wrong fold and it crumbles.'

influence:0.en: Silverfang placed a polished stone on the table and claimed it could *influence* the direction of any wind current around the islands. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. I watched the small stone catch the lantern light and spin slowly, as if agreeing with everything Silverfang said.
influence:0.cnHint: 竞争船长声称那颗石头能____风向，但老舵手并不相信。
influence:0.hook: Then the lantern flame bent sharply toward the stone.
influence:0.line: 'That stone can *influence* even the oldest storm, I promise you.'

argue:0.en: Old Helm and Silverfang stood on opposite sides of the map table and began to *argue* about which route would reach the next island before nightfall. Their voices rose and filled the small cabin. Bell caught my eye and gave a small, tired smile, as if this happened every single evening.
argue:0.cnHint: 老舵手和竞争船长为走哪条路线而激烈____，小铃对此早已习以为常。
argue:0.hook: Neither noticed the route shifting on the map below them.
argue:0.line: 'I will *argue* this point until the stars go out, old man.'

pass:0.en: Bell called for quiet, then asked each of us to *pass* our word-fragments to her one by one. She lined them up along the table's edge in an order only she seemed to understand. When the last piece arrived, a soft hum rose from the row, and the cabin felt lighter.
pass:0.cnHint: 小铃让大家把各自的词语碎片____给她，她要按某种顺序排列它们。
pass:0.hook: The hum grew louder the moment all pieces touched.
pass:0.line: '*Pass* me yours gently — these fragments remember being broken.'

serious:0.en: The laughter in the cabin faded when Silverfang set down his cup and looked at us with *serious* eyes. He said the next island demanded something more than clever words — it demanded courage. No one moved. Even the lantern seemed to dim, as though it too understood the weight of what lay ahead.
serious:0.cnHint: 竞争船长突然变得____，告诉大家前方的岛屿需要的不只是智慧。
serious:0.hook: Outside, the wind dropped to perfect, unsettling silence.
serious:0.line: 'I am *serious* — turn back now, or give me your full trust.'

despite:0.en: *Despite* a torn corner and a water stain across its middle, the old chart still showed the way clearly enough. Old Helm traced the path with one careful finger while Bell copied each turn into her small notebook. I felt a quiet pride watching them work around every flaw without complaint.
despite:0.cnHint: ____地图残破不堪，老舵手和小铃还是从中找到了前进的方向。
despite:0.hook: The stain, we then saw, was not water at all.
despite:0.line: '*Despite* the damage, this map has never once lied to us.'

express:0.en: I wanted to thank Old Helm for letting me join the troupe, but I could not find the right words. He must have noticed, because he smiled before I could speak. 'You don't need words,' he said gently. 'Your eyes *express* everything already.' I looked away, warm to the ears.
express:0.cnHint: 我想感谢老舵手，却不知如何开口，他说我的眼神已经____了一切。
express:0.hook: He then handed me the troupe's oldest map to keep.
express:0.line: 'Your eyes *express* more than any word ever could, young one.'

conduct:0.en: The card game was already in progress when I stepped inside the lantern-lit cabin. Silverfang sat across from Old Helm, coins stacked between them. Bell leaned against the wall, watching. 'Your *conduct* at this table tells me everything,' Old Helm said, studying Silverfang's face the way a sailor studies clouds.
conduct:0.cnHint: 在小屋里，老舵观察银牙在牌桌上的____，试图看穿他的心思。
conduct:0.hook: Silverfang smiled, and not one coin moved.
conduct:0.line: 'Your *conduct* at this table tells me everything,' Old Helm said calmly.

reveal:0.en: The bet was a folded paper — Silverfang's copy of a star chart, or so he claimed. Old Helm placed a worn key on the table in return. Bell held her breath. Silverfang slowly opened the paper to *reveal* a single word glowing like a small sun: MERIDIAN. The room went very quiet.
reveal:0.cnHint: 银牙打开纸张，____出一个发光的词语，整个船舱陷入沉默。
reveal:0.hook: Old Helm's hand closed over the key before anyone else could move.
reveal:0.line: 'Allow me to *reveal* what I actually wagered,' Silverfang said softly.

powerful:0.en: Old Helm lost the first round. He did not look worried. 'A *powerful* word is worth more than a pile of coins,' he told me afterward, sorting the tokens with one steady hand. Silverfang watched from across the table, trying to decide if that was wisdom or a bluff. So was I.
powerful:0.cnHint: 老舵输掉第一局后，平静地说一个____的词比一堆金币更有价值。
powerful:0.hook: Silverfang pushed every coin he had to the centre of the table.
powerful:0.line: 'A *powerful* word opens doors that coins never could,' Old Helm said.

push:0.en: Bell calculated the odds on a small chalkboard while the others played. With one round left, Old Helm needed a final *push* — a bold move that could win the chart or lose the key forever. I watched him take a slow breath and lay his last card face-up on the table.
push:0.cnHint: 最后一局，老舵需要一次关键的____才能赢得那张星图。
push:0.hook: The card caught the lantern light, and nobody breathed.
push:0.line: 'One more *push* and this game is ours,' Old Helm said quietly.

wonder:0.en: Nobody spoke for a long moment after the final card fell. I felt a *wonder* I could not name — not just at who had won, but at the word now sitting in Old Helm's palm, glowing faintly gold, pointing to an island none of us had ever seen on any map before tonight.
wonder:0.cnHint: 游戏结束后，我心中涌起一种____，因为那个词指向了一座从未见过的岛屿。
wonder:0.hook: Old Helm closed his fingers around the word, and the lantern dimmed.
wonder:0.line: 'Is it any *wonder* that a single word can change our whole journey?' Bell asked.

design:0.en: Bell spread a fresh sheet of paper and began to *design* a route using the new word as a fixed point. Her pen moved with quiet confidence, linking islands in an arc that swept far beyond our old maps. Silverfang watched, tapping the table once — the only compliment he seemed willing to give.
design:0.cnHint: 小铃开始____一条以新词为基准的航线，将地图延伸到从未到达的地方。
design:0.hook: One island on the new route had no name — only a question mark.
design:0.line: 'Let me *design* the route tonight so we can leave at first light,' Bell said.

exercise:0.en: After the game, Old Helm made me *exercise* my memory by reciting every word the troupe had collected so far. Standing in the small cabin, I spoke each one aloud. Each syllable seemed to light a faint point on the ceiling, like stars being placed one by one into a private sky.
exercise:0.cnHint: 游戏结束后，老舵让我通过背诵所有词语来____记忆力。
exercise:0.hook: When I finished, a pattern of lights on the ceiling showed a path.
exercise:0.line: '*Exercise* your memory every night — that is how a word stays alive,' Old Helm said.

space:0.en: The winning word, MERIDIAN, needed its own *space* on the map board — a clear gap between the known islands and the unknown. Bell pinned it there carefully, and for a moment the blank area around it felt less like emptiness and more like a held breath, waiting for us to arrive and fill it.
space:0.cnHint: 小铃把新词钉在地图上，为它留出一片____，那里是尚未踏足的未知之地。
space:0.hook: The blank space around MERIDIAN began, very slowly, to glow.
space:0.line: 'Leave *space* beside it — that island is bigger than it first appears,' Bell said.

career:0.en: The back room of Silverfang's ship served as his private quarters. Trophies covered every wall — race flags, broken compasses, cracked lenses. Old Helm picked up a faded flag and smiled. 'Every trophy here marks a turn in his *career*,' he said softly. 'Win or lose, each one carried him forward.' I understood then why Silverfang never threw anything away.
career:0.cnHint: 老舵手指着银牙船舱里满墙的奖杯，讲述了他漫长____的每一个转折点。
career:0.hook: But one trophy had no flag — only a locked iron box beneath it.
career:0.line: 'Every trophy here marks a turn in his *career*,' Old Helm said softly.

medium:0.en: Bell spread a blank chart on the table and held a glowing crystal above it. 'This crystal is our *medium*,' she said. 'Words we collect pass through it and burn their shape into the map.' A soft hiss, and the outline of a new island appeared in pale blue light. The crystal cooled, and the room smelled of open sky.
medium:0.cnHint: 贝尔用一块发光的水晶作为____，让收集到的词语在地图上烧刻出新岛屿的轮廓。
medium:0.hook: The pale blue outline flickered — then split into two separate islands.
medium:0.line: 'This crystal is our *medium*,' Bell said, holding it above the blank chart.

office:0.en: Silverfang called the wide captain's cabin at the bow his *office*. Charts hung from every beam, and a brass lamp swung with the wind. He sat behind a heavy desk, fingers laced, watching me with one raised eyebrow. 'You want to join the bet?' he asked. The lamp swung. Shadows crossed his face like passing clouds.
office:0.cnHint: 银牙把船头那间挂满地图的船舱当作他的____，在那里向我提出了那个赌约。
office:0.hook: He slid a sealed envelope across the desk without another word.
office:0.line: 'Welcome to my *office*,' Silverfang said, gesturing at the chart-covered walls.

culture:0.en: Old Helm unwrapped a small painted tile from his coat. 'Every island has its own *culture*,' he said, setting it gently on the table. 'This tile is how the Cloud Weavers greet a guest — colour first, then shape, then silence.' I turned it over. The back held a single word, still warm, still glowing faintly gold.
culture:0.cnHint: 老舵手展示了一块彩绘瓷砖，说每座岛都有独特的____，这块砖是云织者迎客的方式。
culture:0.hook: The word on the tile's back matched none we had collected — yet.
culture:0.line: 'Every island has its own *culture*,' Old Helm said, setting the tile down gently.

college:0.en: A stack of old notebooks filled one shelf of Silverfang's cabin. Bell pulled one out and blew off the dust. 'He studied at the Sky *College* before he ever raced,' she told me, almost whispering. The pages were full of careful drawings — wind patterns, star angles, tide curves. I looked at Silverfang differently after that.
college:0.cnHint: 贝尔从架子上取下一本旧笔记本，告诉我银牙曾在天空____里认真学习过。
college:0.hook: The last page of the notebook held a map no one had ever seen before.
college:0.line: 'He studied at the Sky *College* long before he ever raced,' Bell whispered.

value:0.en: Silverfang dropped a small amber stone on the table between us. 'Name its *value*,' he said. Old Helm leaned in close, then shook his head slowly. 'You can't count it in gold,' Old Helm replied. 'It holds a memory — the first word this troupe ever found.' The stone pulsed once, warm and quiet, and the whole cabin felt lighter.
value:0.cnHint: 银牙把一块琥珀石放在桌上，让老舵手说出它的____，而那枚石头里藏着船队最初的记忆。
value:0.hook: Then Silverfang smiled and said the stone was the prize of his bet.
value:0.line: 'Name its *value*,' Silverfang said, sliding the amber stone across the table.

connection:0.en: Bell traced two lines on the chart with her finger — one from our island, one from Silverfang's last known port. They met at a blank space. 'There's a *connection* between these two routes,' she said, voice rising with excitement. 'Follow both and they lead to the same hidden peak.' Old Helm pressed his thumb to the crossing point, and the map shimmered.
connection:0.cnHint: 贝尔在地图上发现两条航线之间有____，它们交汇处隐藏着一座从未记录的山峰。
connection:0.hook: The hidden peak had a name already written — in our own handwriting.
connection:0.line: 'There is a *connection* between these two routes,' Bell said, her voice lifting.

story:0.en: The bet began, Silverfang explained, with a *story* — an old one, told on this very island before any of us were born. A captain had hidden a word so powerful it could open ten islands at once. Old Helm nodded slowly. 'I know that story,' he murmured. 'I just never believed it was true.' Outside, the stars burned a little brighter.
story:0.cnHint: 银牙说这场赌约源于一个古老的____，讲述着一个能同时开启十座岛屿的神秘词语。
story:0.hook: Old Helm's hand trembled slightly as he set down his cup.
story:0.line: 'It all began with a *story*,' Silverfang said, 'told here before we were born.'

sign:0.en: Inside the map room of Silverfang's ship, dusty charts covered every wall. Old Helm traced a strange mark with one finger. 'That *sign* means danger ahead,' he said quietly. Bell leaned closer, eyes wide. Outside, the wind had gone completely still.
sign:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里发现了一个不寻常的____，提醒大家前方有危险。
sign:0.hook: The stillness outside was not peace — it was a warning.
sign:0.line: 'That *sign* on the chart — I have seen it once before.'

feeling:0.en: Silverfang poured two cups of warm tea and pushed one across the table to Old Helm. 'I have a *feeling* you already know what the bet is,' she said, smiling just a little. Old Helm wrapped both hands around his cup and said nothing for a long moment.
feeling:0.cnHint: 银牙在室内提出赌约时，老舵手对她的意图有一种强烈的____。
feeling:0.hook: His silence told her everything she needed to know.
feeling:0.line: 'My *feeling* says this bet is not as simple as it sounds.'

professional:0.en: Bell spread her navigation tools across the table in a neat row. 'A *professional* always checks twice,' she said, adjusting a small compass. Silverfang watched from across the room, arms folded. She was clearly measuring Bell — not just her tools, but the steady hands holding them.
professional:0.cnHint: 领航员贝尔用____的态度摆好工具，悄悄赢得了银牙的注意。
professional:0.hook: Silverfang unfolded her arms — a rare and telling gesture.
professional:0.line: 'A *professional* never rushes, even when the clock is running.'

behind:0.en: Old Helm set his tea down slowly. 'We are *behind* by three word-fragments,' he admitted, smoothing the chart with his palm. Bell bit her lip. Silverfang's crew had found two islands already. The gap felt wider than the stars above, and the bet had only just begun.
behind:0.cnHint: 老舵手坦承我们的碎片数量____银牙的队伍，形势不妙。
behind:0.hook: Three fragments behind — and the next island would not wait.
behind:0.line: 'We are *behind*, yes — but the last island has not been claimed.'

government:0.en: Bell pointed to a faded seal at the corner of the old chart. 'This stamp belongs to the sky *government* — the council that once ruled all the floating islands,' she said. Silverfang raised an eyebrow. If the council's routes were hidden in these maps, the bet had just become something far larger.
government:0.cnHint: 贝尔在地图上发现了天空____的印章，暗示这份赌约牵涉更大的秘密。
government:0.hook: A council that once ruled everything — and then vanished without trace.
government:0.line: 'The sky *government* sealed these routes for a reason nobody remembers.'

growth:0.en: Silverfang tapped a cluster of tiny symbols on the chart. 'See this pattern? It marks rapid *growth* — new islands forming where two wind currents cross,' she explained. Old Helm leaned in, genuinely surprised. He had sailed these skies for decades and had never noticed the pattern before tonight.
growth:0.cnHint: 银牙指出地图上记录岛屿____规律的符号，令老舵手大感意外。
growth:0.hook: New islands meant new words — and whoever found them first would win.
growth:0.line: 'The *growth* here is recent — these islands did not exist ten years ago.'

negative:0.en: Old Helm studied the proposed route and shook his head. 'My answer is *negative*,' he said firmly, setting the chart down. 'This path cuts too close to the dead winds.' Silverfang tilted her head, clearly expecting a different reply. Bell glanced between them, her pencil frozen above the page.
negative:0.cnHint: 老舵手对银牙提出的航线给出了____的回应，双方陷入僵局。
negative:0.hook: A flat refusal — but Silverfang was already pulling out a second chart.
negative:0.line: 'My answer is *negative* — unless you can show me a safer pass.'

potential:0.en: Silverfang rolled up the chart and held it out to Old Helm. 'This fragment has *potential* — it could lead to three new islands at once,' she said, her voice low and certain. Old Helm looked at the roll of paper, then at her eyes. He reached out and took it slowly.
potential:0.cnHint: 银牙认为这份碎片有巨大的____，老舵手迟疑片刻后还是接了过来。
potential:0.hook: One small roll of paper — and a whole sky of unknowns inside.
potential:0.line: 'Its *potential* is exactly why I am offering it as the prize.'

force:0.en: Inside the map room, Silverfang slammed a brass key onto the table. 'You will hand over the northern fragment,' he said. Old Helm crossed his arms. No threat could *force* him to give up the troupe's only route across the storm belt. I held my breath.
force:0.cnHint: 银牙试图____老舵手交出地图碎片，但老舵手毫不退让。
force:0.hook: The key scraped the table — and something beneath it clicked.
force:0.line: 'Nothing will *force* me to abandon my crew's only path forward.'

importance:0.en: Bell spread the recovered charts across the low table, tracing each floating island with a careful finger. She spoke quietly about the *importance* of reading wind patterns before any crossing. Silverfang leaned in, suddenly less the rival and more the student. Even Old Helm nodded slowly.
importance:0.cnHint: 贝尔向大家解释掌握风向规律的____，连银牙也认真听了起来。
importance:0.hook: Then Bell pointed to one blank square none of them could explain.
importance:0.line: 'The *importance* of these wind marks cannot be overstated, believe me.'

sell:0.en: Silverfang laid three glowing word-stones on the table with a theatrical smile. 'A *sell* I regret already,' he admitted, 'but I need your northern charts more than these.' Old Helm studied the stones in silence. Outside, the wind shifted, as if the sky itself were listening.
sell:0.cnHint: 银牙把三块发光词石拿出来交换，却说这笔____让他心里不是滋味。
sell:0.hook: One of the stones pulsed once — then went completely dark.
sell:0.line: 'This *sell* stings, but a fair trade is a fair trade.'

replace:0.en: The old compass on the shelf had cracked during the last crossing. Silverfang pulled a newer one from his coat. 'I can *replace* it — at a price,' he said, setting it beside the broken one. Bell glanced at me. We both knew the price would not be small.
replace:0.cnHint: 银牙提出可以____破损的罗盘，但他的要价让众人心生警惕。
replace:0.hook: He named the price, and the lantern above us flickered.
replace:0.line: 'I can *replace* that compass — but you will owe me one favour.'

approach:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a worn scroll and tapped it twice. 'Our *approach* to every new island is the same: we listen before we land,' he said. Silverfang snorted. I watched them both, wondering which method would carry us safely past the fog wall looming on the eastern edge.
approach:0.cnHint: 老舵手说明了抵达每座新岛时一贯的____，银牙却不以为然。
approach:0.hook: The fog wall on the scroll seemed to shift under the lamplight.
approach:0.line: 'Our *approach* has kept this troupe alive longer than yours has sailed.'

engage:0.en: Bell suggested we *engage* Silverfang in a wager rather than an argument. 'Winner reads the next map fragment first,' she said brightly. The room felt lighter at once. Even Silverfang uncrossed his arms. Old Helm allowed himself a small smile and reached for the sealed envelope on the shelf.
engage:0.cnHint: 贝尔建议用打赌的方式让银牙____进来，化解了剑拔弩张的气氛。
engage:0.hook: The sealed envelope had someone else's name written on the back.
engage:0.line: 'Let us *engage* in a fair wager and settle this cleanly.'

ensure:0.en: Before the debate went any further, I quietly moved the troupe's master log to the inner drawer and locked it. Old Helm caught my eye and gave the smallest nod. It was the only way to *ensure* nothing valuable would vanish during Silverfang's visit to the map room.
ensure:0.cnHint: 我悄悄锁好航行总记录，以____银牙离开后重要资料不会丢失。
ensure:0.hook: But when I turned back, the drawer key was already gone.
ensure:0.line: 'We must *ensure* the records stay safe while our guest is here.'

limit:0.en: Silverfang spread his hands wide. 'I have reached my *limit*,' he said, almost gently. 'One more word-stone and nothing else.' Old Helm studied him for a long moment, then rolled up the eastern chart. I felt the whole room exhale. A boundary had been drawn in the lamplight.
limit:0.cnHint: 银牙宣布自己的底线，说明了他所能接受的____，谈判气氛随之缓和。
limit:0.hook: Old Helm smiled, rolled the chart back open, and said nothing.
limit:0.line: 'One stone is my *limit* — push further and the deal is done.'

real:0.en: Inside Silverfang's ship, shelves lined every wall, each holding a glowing word-stone. I reached for the nearest one, but Old Helm caught my wrist. 'Look closer,' he said. Half the stones were painted glass — fakes. Only one shelf held *real* word-stones, pulsing with warm gold light.
real:0.cnHint: 老舵手提醒我，银牙船上的词石大多是假的，只有一排是____的。
real:0.hook: But which shelf held the one we needed?
real:0.line: 'These *real* stones are the only ones worth trading for.'

talk:0.en: Silverfang spread a star-chart across the table and tapped it twice. 'Sit,' he said, not unkindly. Old Helm pulled out a chair, and I followed. The three of us leaned over the glowing map. This was no ordinary *talk* — every word felt like a move in a quiet, careful game.
talk:0.cnHint: 银牙邀我们围坐在星图前，展开了一场不寻常的____。
talk:0.hook: Then Silverfang smiled and turned the chart face-down.
talk:0.line: 'This *talk* decides who sails to the next island first.'

energy:0.en: Bell pressed her ear to the engine-room wall and frowned. The ship hummed, but weakly. 'The word-core is fading,' she said. Without its *energy*, the floating island below us would begin to sink before dawn. Old Helm looked at me, and I understood — we had very little time.
energy:0.cnHint: 领航员发现船的词核快没____了，岛屿可能天亮前就会下沉。
energy:0.hook: A low groan shook the floor beneath our feet.
energy:0.line: 'Without *energy* from the word-core, we all fall tonight.'

plan:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a small piece of cloth on Silverfang's table. Tiny symbols covered it in neat rows. 'This is our *plan*,' he said quietly. Silverfang crossed his arms but did not look away. Bell traced one symbol with her finger. Outside, the stars shifted — time, I realised, was already moving.
plan:0.cnHint: 老舵手在银牙面前展开布条，说出了我们的____。
plan:0.hook: Silverfang's finger stopped on the one symbol none of us recognised.
plan:0.line: 'Your *plan* is bold — I did not think you had it in you.'

bear:0.en: The old chest in the corner had not been opened in years; its lock was stiff with rust. Silverfang lifted the lid at last, and we all held our breath. Inside lay a word-stone heavier than any I had seen. 'Can you *bear* the weight of it?' Old Helm asked me softly.
bear:0.cnHint: 银牙打开旧箱子，老舵手问我能不能____那枚词石的重量。
bear:0.hook: The stone pulsed once — and then went completely dark.
bear:0.line: 'I can *bear* it — just give me a moment to steady myself.'

organization:0.en: Silverfang slid a painted badge across the table. It showed a ring of five islands around a single star. 'Every ship that sails the upper sky belongs to an *organization*,' he said. 'Every troupe, too — whether they know it or not.' Old Helm stared at the badge as if he recognised the star.
organization:0.cnHint: 银牙展示一枚徽章，暗示每支队伍都属于某个____。
organization:0.hook: Old Helm's hand closed over the badge before I could read it.
organization:0.line: 'Our *organization* has watched your troupe for three seasons now.'

opportunity:0.en: 'You came at the right moment,' Silverfang said, refilling our cups without being asked. 'The sky-gate opens only once each month. That is your *opportunity* — and mine.' He smiled, and the lamp above us swayed as if the whole ship had heard him. Bell caught my eye across the table and gave one small nod.
opportunity:0.cnHint: 银牙说天门每月只开一次，这是我们难得的____。
opportunity:0.hook: He slid a second cup toward an empty chair — someone was still coming.
opportunity:0.line: 'Miss this *opportunity* and you wait another full month in the cold.'

professor:0.en: On the highest shelf sat a portrait — an old figure in a wide hat, surrounded by open books. 'Who is that?' I asked. Silverfang glanced up. 'A *professor* from the ground-cities, long ago. He mapped the first floating island and lost himself looking for the second.' Old Helm said nothing, but his jaw tightened.
professor:0.cnHint: 银牙船舱最高处挂着一位____的画像，老舵手见到它神情微变。
professor:0.hook: The figure in the portrait seemed to be pointing at exactly where we stood.
professor:0.line: 'That *professor* knew more about the sky-islands than anyone alive — or so we thought.'

perhaps:0.en: Inside the map-room of Silverfang's sky-ship, charts covered every wall. Old Helm spread the newest fragment on the table and studied it in silence. 'This symbol near the eastern edge,' he said slowly, 'is *perhaps* a door — or a warning. We cannot tell which until we stand before it.'
perhaps:0.cnHint: 老舵主盯着地图碎片上的神秘符号，认为它____是一扇门，也____是一个警告。
perhaps:0.hook: Either way, the troupe would reach it by dawn.

video:0.en: Bell had built a small light-box that could replay scenes from the past. She called it her *video* lantern. Inside the map-room she played a clip showing the lost island of Auren, its towers still whole, its lights still burning. Every member of the troupe leaned in, breath held.
video:0.cnHint: 领航员用她的____灯笼，在地图室里重放了那座消失岛屿昔日的景象。
video:0.hook: The towers in the clip had already begun to flicker.
video:0.line: 'Watch the *video* lantern closely — the island still breathes.'

prevent:0.en: Silverfang slammed the iron door of the map-room shut and bolted it. 'Three locks,' he said, 'should *prevent* anyone from stealing the star-charts tonight.' Old Helm raised an eyebrow. Outside, the wind had already begun to whistle through the cracks in a very deliberate way.
prevent:0.cnHint: 竞争船长用三把锁____他人偷走星图，但那阵风听起来不像是普通的风。
prevent:0.hook: A key scraped softly against the lock from outside.
prevent:0.line: 'Three bolts will *prevent* any thief tonight — I am certain.'

source:0.en: Deep in the ship's lower deck, Bell found a small glowing stone wedged behind a beam. 'This is the *source* of the humming we have heard for days,' she whispered. The stone pulsed like a heartbeat, and faint letters rose from its surface — the beginning of a new map fragment.
source:0.cnHint: 领航员在甲板底层找到了那块神秘嗡鸣声的____，发现它正是下一张地图碎片的起点。
source:0.hook: The letters spelled a name none of them recognised.
source:0.line: 'I found the *source* of the hum — and it wants to be read.'

available:0.en: Old Helm searched every shelf in the map-room for a spare compass needle, but only one was *available* — bent at the tip and older than the ship itself. He straightened it carefully against the edge of the table. Silverfang watched with crossed arms, clearly doubting it would ever point true.
available:0.cnHint: 老舵主发现整个地图室里只有一根弯曲的指南针针可____，但他仍决定用它。
available:0.hook: The bent needle spun once, then locked onto a direction no chart showed.
available:0.line: 'Only one compass needle is *available*, and I intend to trust it.'

customer:0.en: A hooded figure knocked at the map-room door and introduced himself as a *customer* looking to trade a cloud-stone for safe passage to the next island. Old Helm let him in with a careful smile. Bell noticed the figure's boots were still damp — from which rain, on which island, she could not say.
customer:0.cnHint: 一位神秘____来到地图室，用云石换取前往下座岛屿的安全通道，但他靴子上的水迹让领航员起了疑心。
customer:0.hook: No rain had fallen anywhere near the ship for three days.
customer:0.line: 'I am a *customer* with fair trade — a cloud-stone for safe passage.'

language:0.en: The new map fragment was covered in writing, but it was no *language* anyone in the troupe could read. Bell traced each symbol with her finger while Old Helm flipped through every book on the shelf. Silverfang sat apart, pretending not to care, yet his eyes kept drifting back to the page.
language:0.cnHint: 新地图碎片上满是没人认识的____，连竞争船长也忍不住偷偷瞄了好几眼。
language:0.hook: Then one symbol glowed the moment Bell whispered her own name.
language:0.line: 'This *language* is alive — it just lit up when I spoke.'

test:0.en: Silverfang laid three numbered tiles on the map-room table and said the fragment would only open to someone who passed his *test*: choose the tile hiding the true compass-point, and the chart is yours for the night. Old Helm studied the tiles without touching them, then tapped the middle one without a word.
test:0.cnHint: 竞争船长设下一道____，只有选出正确的指南针方位牌，才能借得星图。
test:0.hook: Silverfang's smile faded — that was exactly the tile he had hoped no one would pick.
test:0.line: 'Pass my *test* and the chart is yours until sunrise — do you dare?'

save:0.en: The card game had gone on for an hour inside Silverfang's warm cabin. I watched Old Helm push his last coin forward. Then Bell slid a folded note across the table. 'You don't need to *save* your pride,' Bell said softly, 'just your coins.' Old Helm laughed, pocketed the note, and folded his hand.
save:0.cnHint: 在银牙的船舱里，赌局正酣，贝尔悄悄提醒老舵主要____自己的硬币。
save:0.hook: But the note in Old Helm's pocket held more than advice.
save:0.line: 'You don't need to *save* your pride — just your coins.'

service:0.en: Silverfang's cabin doubled as a small inn for sky-traders. A chalkboard on the wall listed every *service* on offer — hot soup, star-charts, ink for writing new words. I traced the list with one finger, amazed that one tiny room could hold so much warmth for so many travellers passing through.
service:0.cnHint: 银牙的船舱兼做小旅店，墙上黑板列出了所有的____项目。
service:0.hook: One item on the list was crossed out — and nobody would say why.
service:0.line: 'Every *service* on that board is real — yes, even the star-charts.'

note:0.en: Bell spread a hand-drawn map across Silverfang's table. Each island was marked with a tiny *note* — a single word written in careful ink. 'Each one is a clue,' Bell explained, tapping the nearest mark. I leaned in close and read the word aloud. A soft chime filled the cabin, and one corner of the map began to glow.
note:0.cnHint: 贝尔把地图铺开，每座岛上都有一个小小的____，写着一个单词线索。
note:0.hook: The glowing corner pointed toward an island none of them had named.
note:0.line: 'Read the *note* on each island aloud — the map will do the rest.'

probably:0.en: Silverfang tossed three coins onto the table and grinned. 'This island is *probably* the richest stop on the whole route,' he said, 'if you know where to look.' Old Helm raised an eyebrow. I pulled out my word-journal and wrote the word down carefully, already imagining what richness might mean on a floating island full of stars.
probably:0.cnHint: 银牙把硬币扔上桌，说这座岛____是整条航线最富饶的一站。
probably:0.hook: Old Helm's eyebrow stayed raised — he had heard that claim before.
probably:0.line: 'This stop is *probably* the richest on the whole route — trust me.'

strategy:0.en: The card game was not really about cards. Silverfang leaned back and explained his *strategy*: lose small early, let others grow bold, then win the one hand that mattered. I scribbled the word into my journal. Old Helm smiled across the table. 'Sounds like navigating a storm,' he said. Silverfang just dealt the next round.
strategy:0.cnHint: 银牙解释了他玩牌的____：先小输，再赢最关键的一局。
strategy:0.hook: Old Helm's smile suggested he had already seen through the whole plan.
strategy:0.line: 'A good *strategy* is the same at cards as it is crossing a storm.'

building:0.en: Through the porthole I could see the nearest island clearly. At its centre stood one tall *building*, lit from within, its windows shaped like open books. 'That is the word-hall,' Bell said, appearing beside me. 'Every word the troupe has ever collected is kept there.' My breath fogged the glass.
building:0.cnHint: 透过舷窗，我看见最近那座岛中央有一栋____，贝尔说那是存放所有词语的大厅。
building:0.hook: The light inside the building flickered — once, twice — then held steady.
building:0.line: 'That *building* holds every word we have ever found — all of them.'

community:0.en: Silverfang described the island ahead as a *community* of sky-traders, scholars, and star-watchers who had all chosen to live together above the clouds. 'They share everything,' he said, 'maps, meals, even words.' I looked at Old Helm and Bell beside me and realised, quietly, that our small troupe was a community too.
community:0.cnHint: 银牙描述前方岛屿是一个____，云上的商人、学者和观星者共同生活。
community:0.hook: Somewhere in that community, someone was already expecting us.
community:0.line: 'A *community* that shares its words never loses its way.'

internet:0.en: Bell pulled out a strange flat stone that hummed faintly. 'The sky-scholars call it the *internet* of islands,' Bell said, 'every stone is linked, and a word spoken into one is heard by all.' I pressed my ear close and heard distant voices trading new words across the dark. Old Helm smiled. 'Add it to the journal.'
internet:0.cnHint: 贝尔拿出一块嗡嗡作响的石板，说岛屿间有一张____，每块石板都相互相连。
internet:0.hook: One of the distant voices spoke a word that was not on any map yet.
internet:0.line: 'The scholars call this the *internet* of islands — every stone is linked.'

seek:0.en: The card room on Silverfang's ship smelled of lamp oil and old wood. Silverfang spread a worn chart across the table. 'Every captain must *seek* the next island,' he said, tapping a blank corner of the map. Old Helm nodded slowly. I held my breath, feeling the blank space pull at me like a question waiting to be answered.
seek:0.cnHint: 银牙船长在船舱里展开地图，说每个船长都必须____下一座岛屿。
seek:0.hook: The blank corner of the map began to glow.
seek:0.line: 'Every captain must *seek* the next island — or the map stays dark.'

exist:0.en: Bell lit a small lantern and hung it from the cabin beam. 'Does the island of Mirrorholt really *exist*?' I asked. She smiled and opened a logbook to a page filled with tiny drawings — towers, bridges, star-shaped pools. 'These were drawn by someone who stood there,' she said. The lantern flame dipped as if agreeing.
exist:0.cnHint: 贝尔打开航海日志，向讲述者证明那座神秘岛屿确实____。
exist:0.hook: A second logbook fell open to the very same page.
exist:0.line: 'Yes, it does *exist* — I copied these drawings from the last navigator.'

supply:0.en: Old Helm counted tins on the storeroom shelf, his lips moving quietly. 'Our *supply* of star-salt is running low,' he announced, clicking the last tin shut. Bell marked something on her list. Silverfang leaned in the doorway, arms crossed, wearing the look of a man who already had a plan. The shelf creaked in the silence.
supply:0.cnHint: 团长在储藏室清点物资，发现星盐的____不足了。
supply:0.hook: Silverfang's plan involved a market no one had visited in years.
supply:0.line: 'The *supply* of star-salt runs out by dawn — we trade tonight.'

visit:0.en: 'This will be my third *visit* to the Isle of Echoes,' Silverfang said, dropping into a chair and propping his boots on the table. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. 'You never mentioned going twice before.' Silverfang just shrugged and studied his cup. I stared at the map and wondered what he had left out of the story.
visit:0.cnHint: 银牙提到这将是他第三次____回声岛，但团长发现他从未提过前两次。
visit:0.hook: Old Helm pulled out a record that named only two captains who had ever returned.
visit:0.line: 'My third *visit* to that island, and I still don't understand what it wants.'

worry:0.en: I spread my notes across the bunk and stared at them. Bell appeared at the door. 'You look like a knot,' she said. 'What's the *worry*?' I told her I was afraid of choosing the wrong word-fragment and sending us off course. She sat beside me, picked up one note, and said, 'Then we choose together.' The knot loosened a little.
worry:0.cnHint: 讲述者独自整理笔记，贝尔看出了他的____并坐下来陪他一起面对。
worry:0.hook: Outside, the wind shifted, and the ship turned without anyone touching the wheel.
worry:0.line: 'Tell me the *worry* — keeping it quiet only makes it louder.'

adapt:0.en: The new word-fragment glowed purple instead of the usual gold. 'Strange colour,' I said. Old Helm turned it over in his hands. 'Some words *adapt* to the island that holds them — they take on its colour.' He set it on the chart and it pulsed once, drawing a thin line toward the western edge of the map. None of us had ever sailed west before.
adapt:0.cnHint: 团长解释，有些词碎片会____成持有它的岛屿的颜色。
adapt:0.hook: The thin line on the map kept growing while we slept.
adapt:0.line: 'Words *adapt* to where they've been kept — that purple means something cold and high.'

bit:0.en: Silverfang pushed a small box across the table toward Old Helm. Inside was a *bit* of pale stone, no bigger than a thumbnail, carved with a single letter. 'Found it in the wall of the lower cabin,' Silverfang said. Old Helm picked it up and held it to the light. His eyes went wide in a way I had never seen before.
bit:0.cnHint: 银牙从船舱墙壁里找到一小____刻有字母的石头，让团长大吃一惊。
bit:0.hook: The letter carved in the stone was not from any alphabet Bell recognised.
bit:0.line: 'Just a *bit* of stone — but look at what it's carved with.'

check:0.en: Bell ran her finger down the navigation log and paused. 'I need to *check* one entry before we set course,' she said, pulling a second log from the shelf. She compared two pages side by side, tracing lines with her nail. Then she looked up with a quiet smile. 'The route is safe. Someone made this crossing before us and wrote it all down.'
check:0.cnHint: 贝尔在出发前____航行记录，发现前人已经走过这条路。
check:0.hook: The handwriting in the second log matched no one in the crew.
check:0.line: 'Let me *check* this entry first — I'd rather be sure than fast.'

stick:0.en: Inside Silverfang's trading cabin, every wall was covered with small notes. Old Helm pointed to a map pinned at the centre. 'The troupe must *stick* to this route,' he said, pressing his finger firmly on the paper. I watched the note curl at the edges but hold fast.
stick:0.cnHint: 老船长在银牙的船舱里，将手指按在地图上，要求大家____这条航路。
stick:0.hook: But Silverfang's eyes said she had a very different plan.
stick:0.line: 'We *stick* to the route, or we lose everything we've earned.'

effective:0.en: Bell spread her charts across the low table in the cabin. She traced three possible paths to the next island. 'Only one is *effective*,' she said quietly, tapping the middle line. The other two led into cloud layers so thick that even starlight could not pass through.
effective:0.cnHint: 领航员贝尔在图表上指出，只有中间那条路线才是真正____的。
effective:0.hook: Silverfang folded her arms and said nothing, which was worse than disagreement.
effective:0.line: 'Trust me, this is the only *effective* path through the clouds.'

fear:0.en: The cabin lantern swung as a gust shook the hull. I felt a small *fear* settle in my chest — we were betting our only fuel supply on Silverfang's promise. Old Helm must have noticed, because he placed a steady hand on my shoulder without a word.
fear:0.cnHint: 船舱里的灯摇晃起来，我心中涌起一阵____，因为我们把所有燃料都押在了赌约上。
fear:0.hook: Silverfang smiled at my expression as if she had expected it.
fear:0.line: 'A little *fear* is healthy — it keeps you sharp out here.'

hit:0.en: Silverfang slapped a small glowing stone onto the table. It *hit* the wood with a bright ring and slid to a stop in front of Old Helm. 'That is my stake,' she said. The stone pulsed like a held breath, and even Bell leaned closer to look.
hit:0.cnHint: 银牙把一块发光的石头____在桌上，作为赌注推向老船长。
hit:0.hook: Old Helm had not seen a stone like that in thirty years.
hit:0.line: 'Watch how it *hits* the table — that sound means it is real.'

assume:0.en: 'You *assume* I will lose,' Silverfang said, her voice light but pointed. Old Helm spread his hands. 'I assume nothing — I simply read the wind charts.' She laughed at that, short and bright, then pulled a folded page from her coat and set it on the table between them.
assume:0.cnHint: 银牙认为老船长____她会输，但老船长说他只是看了风向图。
assume:0.hook: The folded page held a route none of us had ever seen before.
assume:0.line: 'Do not *assume* you already know what I am offering.'

generally:0.en: Old Helm explained the rules of the bet slowly, turning the glowing stone in his fingers. '*Generally*, a wager like this ends with one side gaining a word-fragment and the other gaining a favour,' he said. I had heard of such deals, but never watched one formed at a table this small.
generally:0.cnHint: 老船长解释说，这类赌约____以一方得到碎片、另一方得到恩惠而告终。
generally:0.hook: Silverfang tapped the stone and asked what made this wager different.
generally:0.line: '*Generally* these bets are simple, but this one is not.'

interaction:0.en: Bell watched the *interaction* between Old Helm and Silverfang the way she watched two air currents meet — with quiet, careful attention. Every word they exchanged shifted the balance a little. I started taking notes on the back of a chart, trying to catch what I might miss.
interaction:0.cnHint: 贝尔仔细观察着老船长与银牙之间的____，就像观察两股气流交汇一样。
interaction:0.hook: My pen stopped when their voices suddenly dropped to a whisper.
interaction:0.line: 'Every *interaction* between those two changes something in the air.'

top:0.en: Silverfang reached up and pulled a small wooden box from the *top* of the shelf behind her. Dust rose in a thin cloud. She set it on the table, fingers resting on the lid, and looked at Old Helm with an expression that mixed pride and something harder to name.
top:0.cnHint: 银牙从身后书架____取下一个落满灰尘的小木盒，放在了桌上。
top:0.hook: None of us had ever seen her open that box before.
top:0.line: 'This has sat on the *top* shelf since the day I won my ship.'

easily:0.en: The card table inside the Amber Lantern inn was crowded with curious travellers. Silverfang spread a map across the worn wood and grinned. 'These routes can *easily* fool a newcomer,' he said. Old Helm studied the lines without blinking, his calm eyes already tracing the trap hidden beneath the ink.
easily:0.cnHint: 在旅店的牌桌上，银牙展开地图，试图____地迷惑老舵手。
easily:0.hook: Old Helm's finger stopped at exactly the wrong spot.
easily:0.line: 'These routes can *easily* fool a newcomer like you.'

protect:0.en: Rain drummed against the inn's shutters. Silverfang slid a small iron box across the table toward Old Helm. 'Whoever holds this compass can *protect* the whole troupe from getting lost,' he said quietly. Bell leaned in from the doorway, eyes wide, sensing that the box carried more weight than its size suggested.
protect:0.cnHint: 银牙把一个铁盒推给老舵手，声称它能____全团队。
protect:0.hook: The compass needle spun, then pointed nowhere at all.
protect:0.line: 'Whoever holds this can *protect* everyone on the islands.'

advantage:0.en: The bet was simple: first to name every island on the blank map wins. Silverfang tapped the parchment with one finger. 'I have the *advantage*,' he said, 'I have sailed these skies twice already.' Old Helm poured two cups of tea, slid one across, and smiled as if he already knew something Silverfang did not.
advantage:0.cnHint: 银牙认为自己有____，因为他已经航行过这片天空两次。
advantage:0.hook: Then Old Helm named an island that appeared on no map.
advantage:0.line: 'I have the *advantage* — I have sailed here twice before.'

break:0.en: They had argued for an hour without reaching any agreement. Bell stepped between the two captains and set a steaming pot of soup on the table with a firm thud. 'Let's take a *break* before someone says something they cannot unsay,' she said cheerfully. The smell of warm broth filled the room, and the tension softened just a little.
break:0.cnHint: 贝儿在两位队长争吵了一个小时后，建议大家____一下。
break:0.hook: But the silence that followed felt heavier than the argument.
break:0.line: 'Let's take a *break* before this goes too far.'

conclude:0.en: Silverfang laid his last card face-up on the table and crossed his arms. Old Helm looked at the full spread of cards, then at the map, then at Silverfang. 'I *conclude*,' Old Helm said gently, 'that you planned this bet long before we ever docked.' Silverfang's grin flickered, just once, before he schooled his face smooth again.
conclude:0.cnHint: 老舵手看完所有的牌后，____出银牙早已策划好了这场赌约。
conclude:0.hook: Silverfang's next words came out one beat too slowly.
conclude:0.line: 'I *conclude* you planned this wager long ago, my friend.'

figure:0.en: Bell sketched a rough map on a napkin while the two captains argued. She had counted every island Silverfang named and every island Old Helm named. 'The *figure* you each keep missing,' she said, holding up the napkin, 'is twelve — there are twelve islands, not eleven.' Both captains fell silent and stared at her drawing.
figure:0.cnHint: 贝儿指出，两位队长报出的____都是错的——岛屿共有十二个。
figure:0.hook: Neither captain could explain where the twelfth island was.
figure:0.line: 'The *figure* you are both missing is twelve, not eleven.'

fit:0.en: Old Helm pulled a worn key from his coat and placed it beside the iron box Silverfang had brought. The key slid into the lock as though it had always belonged there. 'It is a strange thing,' Old Helm said softly, 'when a key seems to *fit* a box you have never seen before.' The room grew very quiet.
fit:0.cnHint: 老舵手拿出一把旧钥匙，它竟然完全____那个铁盒的锁。
fit:0.hook: The lid opened to reveal something none of them expected.
fit:0.line: 'It is strange when a key seems to *fit* a lock like that.'

particular:0.en: Bell spread six charts across the inn table and watched Silverfang's eyes move across them. He paused longest over one *particular* chart — a small one, edged in blue ink, showing a cluster of islands shaped like a crescent. Bell quietly memorised which chart had held his gaze. That chart, she decided, was the one that mattered most.
particular:0.cnHint: 贝儿注意到银牙在某一张____的海图上停留的时间最长。
particular:0.hook: That crescent of islands was not on any other chart.
particular:0.line: 'Why do your eyes keep returning to this *particular* chart?'

consequence:0.en: Inside the map room of Silverfang's ship, scrolls covered every wall. Old Helm studied the wager written on the table. 'Lose this bet,' he said quietly, 'and the *consequence* is we hand over our three best word-fragments.' He folded his hands. No one spoke.
consequence:0.cnHint: 老舵手在银牙的地图室里盯着赌约，说明输掉的____。
consequence:0.hook: Bell's fingers trembled above the sealed contract.
consequence:0.line: 'The *consequence* of losing is too heavy to ignore.'

realize:0.en: The map room smelled of old ink. I watched Silverfang lay out his terms, smiling the whole time. Only when he unrolled the final scroll did I *realize* the bet covered every word-fragment we owned. My stomach dropped straight to the floor.
realize:0.cnHint: 我在地图室里渐渐____到银牙的赌约几乎要夺走我们所有的词语碎片。
realize:0.hook: Old Helm had not moved, but his eyes said everything.
realize:0.line: 'Did you *realize* he wants all of our fragments, not just one?'

mostly:0.en: Silverfang's cabin was *mostly* dark, lit by a single lantern swinging above the table. Maps and coins covered every surface. Bell leaned close to me and whispered that competitions here were usually settled by riddles, not by sword or speed.
mostly:0.cnHint: 银牙的船舱____是黑暗的，小铃悄声告诉我这里的赌约规则。
mostly:0.hook: Then Silverfang placed a strange word-fragment at the centre of the table.
mostly:0.line: 'This ship is *mostly* run on bets and clever words.'

exactly:0.en: Old Helm read the contract aloud, word by word. Silverfang crossed his arms and nodded. 'That is *exactly* what I wrote,' he said, tapping the paper. The wager was clear: whoever named the hidden island first would claim the other crew's rarest fragment.
exactly:0.cnHint: 银牙确认合同内容与他所写的____一致，赌约正式成立。
exactly:0.hook: Neither captain blinked as they reached for the pen.
exactly:0.line: 'That is *exactly* the deal — one fragment, winner takes all.'

vary:0.en: Bell spread three word-fragments on the table and explained that the power of each one could *vary* depending on which island you stood on. Silverfang looked interested. He picked up the smallest fragment and turned it slowly in the lantern light.
vary:0.cnHint: 小铃解释道，每块词语碎片的力量会随地点____，银牙听得很专注。
vary:0.hook: Silverfang's smile widened just a little too much.
vary:0.line: 'The rewards *vary*, but the risk stays the same for us all.'

brain:0.en: The riddle Silverfang read out was short but twisting. I felt my *brain* spin trying to untangle it. Old Helm stayed perfectly still, eyes half closed, breathing slowly, as if the whole noisy cabin belonged to another world far below his thoughts.
brain:0.cnHint: 银牙出了一道谜题，我感到____飞速转动，老舵手却镇定自若。
brain:0.hook: The answer, Old Helm said softly, was already known to me.
brain:0.line: 'Use your *brain*, not your nerves — the answer is in the words.'

stress:0.en: The cabin fell quiet as Old Helm rose to speak. I could feel the *stress* in the air like a hand pressing on my shoulders. Every crew member from both ships watched the table. Outside, wind moved through the rigging with a low hum.
stress:0.cnHint: 船舱里的____让人几乎喘不过气，两船船员都紧盯着谈判桌。
stress:0.hook: Old Helm placed one word-fragment down, face up.
stress:0.line: 'There is no need for *stress* — let the words decide our fate.'

financial:0.en: Silverfang leaned back and said the bet had a *financial* side too: the losing crew would fund the winner's next island crossing. Old Helm raised an eyebrow. Bell quietly did the numbers on a scrap of paper and slid it toward him under the table.
financial:0.cnHint: 银牙提出赌约还附带____条件，小铃悄悄把算好的数字递给老舵手。
financial:0.hook: The number on that scrap of paper made Old Helm's jaw tighten.
financial:0.line: 'The *financial* cost of losing is more than we can spare right now.'

trouble:0.en: Inside the map room, Old Helm spread six torn pieces of parchment across the low table. 'Every island we have missed is marked here,' he said quietly. Silverfang leaned against the wall, arms folded. Finding the missing piece was real *trouble* — without it, the whole route fell apart.
trouble:0.cnHint: 老舵手在地图室里摊开羊皮纸碎片，发现少了关键的一块，这让整个旅程陷入了____。
trouble:0.hook: Someone in this room had seen that piece before.
trouble:0.line: 'This *trouble* is bigger than any storm we have crossed.'

reflect:0.en: Bell held the small compass glass up to the lantern. The flame made tiny patterns dance across the ceiling. 'These light shapes *reflect* where we came from,' she said softly, tracing each one with her finger. Old Helm watched in silence, his eyes wide with something close to hope.
reflect:0.cnHint: 领航员把罗盘玻璃对着灯，让光影____出大家走过的路途。
reflect:0.hook: One pattern pointed somewhere none of them expected.
reflect:0.line: 'Let the light *reflect* the path — it never lies.'

attend:0.en: A folded note had been slipped under the map room door. It read: all crew must *attend* a meeting at the centre table before the next island appears. Old Helm read it twice. Nobody knew who had written it, yet the handwriting looked strangely familiar to Bell.
attend:0.cnHint: 一张神秘字条要求全体船员____一个紧急会议，笔迹却让领航员感到似曾相识。
attend:0.hook: Bell's hand trembled as she set the note down.
attend:0.line: 'We all need to *attend* — whoever wrote this knows our route.'

belief:0.en: Silverfang placed a worn coin on the table beside the map. 'My *belief* is that the missing island moves,' he said, holding Old Helm's gaze. The room went quiet. Even Bell, who doubted almost everything Silverfang said, did not argue this time. The coin spun once, then stopped.
belief:0.cnHint: 银牙在地图旁放下一枚旧硬币，说出了他对失踪岛屿的____，连领航员都沉默了。
belief:0.hook: The coin had stopped pointing at a blank corner of the map.
belief:0.line: 'My *belief* has kept this ship moving — trust it once more.'

carry:0.en: Old Helm asked me to *carry* the rolled map from the shelf to the centre table. It was heavier than it looked. When I unrolled it, three small seeds fell out and scattered across the floor. Bell gasped. She had never seen seeds like those on any island we had visited.
carry:0.cnHint: 老舵手让我____那张卷起的地图，展开后却掉出了三粒从未见过的神秘种子。
carry:0.hook: Bell knelt down and whispered a single island name.
carry:0.line: '*Carry* it gently — that map holds more than paper.'

else:0.en: Silverfang studied the seeds for a long moment, then looked up. 'Someone *else* has been inside this room,' he said, his voice steady but low. Old Helm checked the lock. Bell checked the window latch. Both were shut tight. The lantern flame flickered once without any wind at all.
else:0.cnHint: 银牙盯着那几粒种子，断定曾有____人悄悄进过这个房间，众人顿时警觉起来。
else:0.hook: The locked door had no scratch, yet the seeds were not theirs.
else:0.line: 'Someone *else* knows what we are looking for.'

major:0.en: Inside the troupe's map room, Old Helm spread a dozen glowing word-fragments across the table. 'Most of these lead to small islands,' he said, 'but this one — this is a *major* find.' The fragment pulsed gold, and the whole room seemed to hold its breath.
major:0.cnHint: 老舵手告诉大家，他们找到了一块极其重要的地图碎片，整个地图室都安静了下来。
major:0.hook: No one dared touch the golden fragment — not yet.
major:0.line: 'This is a *major* find — it could open the sky's deepest route.'

communication:0.en: Bell pinned a new word to the board: *communication*. 'On the island of Hush,' she explained, 'the people spoke only in colour. No voice, no writing — just light.' Old Helm nodded slowly. Without a way in, we would be strangers there forever.
communication:0.cnHint: 领航员向大家介绍，一座新岛上的居民用光来进行____，文字和声音都不管用。
communication:0.hook: Bell's fingers hovered over the unlock-slot, and the island shimmered into view.
communication:0.line: '*Communication* on that island means painting the air with colour, not words.'

market:0.en: The word fragment spun open and dropped us into a covered hall full of stalls. Lanterns swayed overhead, and every seller called out in a different tongue. 'A floating *market*,' Bell whispered, eyes wide. Old Helm was already haggling for a new compass needle.
market:0.cnHint: 碎片带着众人来到一座浮空____，每个摊位前都飘着不同语言的叫卖声。
market:0.hook: One stall had no goods on display — only a locked wooden door.
market:0.line: 'Welcome to the floating *market* — everything here was traded for a word.'

apply:0.en: Silverfang held up a small jar of silver paste. 'You have to *apply* this to the hull before we cross the frost belt,' he said, sounding almost proud to know something Old Helm did not. I helped him spread it, and the boards took on a quiet shine.
apply:0.cnHint: 银牙指导大家在船体上____一种银色膏体，以便穿越寒冷地带。
apply:0.hook: The frost belt still glittered ahead — beautiful and unforgiving.
apply:0.line: '*Apply* it evenly — every bare board left uncovered will crack by dawn.'

per:0.en: Old Helm read the island's entry rule aloud: one question *per* visitor, no more. Bell groaned softly. Silverfang straightened his coat as if one careful question was already forming behind his eyes. I had no idea yet what mine would be.
per:0.cnHint: 老舵手宣读了岛屿的规矩：每位访客____人只能提一个问题。
per:0.hook: The gate opened, and suddenly my one question felt very small.
per:0.line: 'One word *per* traveller — spend it wisely and the island rewards you.'

treat:0.en: After a long night of repairs, Old Helm set a warm pot of spiced broth on the table. 'A small *treat*,' he said with a quiet smile, 'for the crew that kept us flying.' The stars outside the porthole seemed brighter somehow, or maybe we were just glad to be warm.
treat:0.cnHint: 修船之后，老舵手为大家准备了一份暖心的____，船员们围坐在一起分享。
treat:0.hook: Bell spotted a new island on the charts — and it had never been named.
treat:0.line: 'Consider this a *treat* — hot broth and a new heading by morning.'

creative:0.en: The island's gate would not open for keys or words. It opened for ideas. Bell laughed when she read the sign. 'Then let's be *creative*,' she said, and began folding a paper bird from the map's edge. It flew straight at the lock, and the gate clicked open.
creative:0.cnHint: 这座岛屿的大门只为有____想法的人开启，领航员用折纸飞鸟打开了它。
creative:0.hook: Inside, the walls were covered in puzzles no one had ever solved.
creative:0.line: 'We have to be *creative* — this gate has never seen the same trick twice.'

perform:0.en: Silverfang crossed his arms and said the word plainly: *perform*. The stage at the island's centre lit up at once. Old Helm blinked. 'I did not expect a theatre,' he murmured. Neither did I — but Bell was already climbing the steps, ready to play her part.
perform:0.cnHint: 银牙说出了关键词，舞台亮起灯光，众人发现这座岛要求访客____一段节目。
perform:0.hook: The audience of empty seats somehow felt like it was waiting just for us.
perform:0.line: 'Every visitor must *perform* one skill — the island remembers each one.'

prepare:0.en: Inside Silverfang's cabin, maps and charts covered every wall. Old Helm spread a worn cloth on the table and began to *prepare* a set of tools — ink brush, compass, and a small brass bowl filled with sky-sand. 'Each word we find needs a proper welcome,' he said softly.
prepare:0.cnHint: 老舵在船舱里仔细____着一套工具，为新收集的词语做好接待的准备。
prepare:0.hook: But one tool was missing, and only I knew where it had gone.
prepare:0.line: 'We must *prepare* every tool before the word arrives, or the map cracks.'

workplace:0.en: Silverfang's navigation deck was more than a bridge — it was his *workplace*, every surface covered with tide charts, hanging lanterns, and little flags marking island positions. Bell stood at the edge, eyes wide. 'I have never seen so many notes in one room,' she whispered.
workplace:0.cnHint: 竞争船长的导航甲板是他的____，密密麻麻贴满了航线图和小旗子。
workplace:0.hook: Then Silverfang walked in and asked which of us had touched his charts.
workplace:0.line: 'A tidy *workplace* means a safe voyage — remember that.'

post:0.en: Old Helm handed me a folded paper and pointed to the wooden board near the cabin door. 'We *post* the new word there so everyone in the troupe can study it before we land,' he explained. The board was already full of earlier words, each pinned with a tiny star-shaped clip.
post:0.cnHint: 老舵让我把新词____在木板上，这样所有团员都能在登陆前学习它。
post:0.hook: Someone had already added a question mark beneath the newest word.
post:0.line: '*Post* it at eye level so no one misses it, please.'

complete:0.en: Bell laid the fragment on the table beside three others. The moment she pressed the fourth piece into place, the map let out a soft hum and glowed faintly gold. 'We *complete* the chart at last,' she breathed, her fingers trembling over the joined edges. Every island name shone like a small star.
complete:0.cnHint: 贝尔将第四块碎片拼上后，地图终于____了，发出温柔的金光。
complete:0.hook: Yet one island on the glowing map had no name at all.
complete:0.line: 'We *complete* the map tonight — tomorrow we sail at dawn.'

measure:0.en: Silverfang knelt beside the cabin wall and held a thin silver rod against a crack in the wood. 'I need to *measure* the gap exactly,' he muttered, squinting at the tiny markings on the rod. Bell watched from the doorway, arms folded. Even the smallest crack, they said, could sink a sky-ship.
measure:0.cnHint: 竞争船长用银杆仔细____船壁上的裂缝，一点偏差都不允许。
measure:0.hook: The number he read made his expression go completely still.
measure:0.line: '*Measure* it twice — a wrong number and we fall through the clouds.'

recommend:0.en: Old Helm pulled a small book from his coat and slid it across the table toward me. 'I *recommend* this guide for anyone who reads a new word for the first time,' he said with a warm smile. The cover showed a floating lantern and the title was just one word: Begin. I opened it carefully.
recommend:0.cnHint: 老舵把一本小册子推给我，____我在学习新词时先读一读它。
recommend:0.hook: The first page was blank except for a single handwritten question.
recommend:0.line: 'I *recommend* you read the first chapter before we reach the next island.'

resource:0.en: 'Water, ink, and sky-sand — these are our most valuable *resource* on a long voyage,' Old Helm said, placing three small jars on the shelf above my bunk. He tapped each one in turn. Without ink the maps could not be drawn; without sky-sand the words would not hold their light. I nodded, understanding the weight of each jar.
resource:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我，水、墨水和星沙是长途旅行中最宝贵的____，缺一不可。
resource:0.hook: That night, one of the jars was found lying on its side, empty.
resource:0.line: 'Guard every *resource* — once it is gone, no island can replace it.'

specific:0.en: Bell spread the chart wide and pointed to a small circle near the edge. 'Old Helm was very *specific*: we must enter this chamber before the third bell or the word inside will fade,' she said. No other time would work, no other door. I checked my pocket watch and felt my heart beat a little faster.
specific:0.cnHint: 贝尔说老舵的指示非常____——必须在第三声钟响前进入那个房间。
specific:0.hook: The second bell had already rung while we were still talking.
specific:0.line: 'Be *specific* about the time — vague plans lose words forever.'

positive:1.en: The market square on Crestholm Island buzzed with colour and noise. Old Helm studied Silverfang's bet-contract, then looked up with bright eyes. 'I'm *positive* this route leads to the Crystal Shelf,' he said, pressing his thumb to the ink seal. The troupe held its breath.
positive:1.cnHint: 老船长仔细审视赌约合同，对航线方向表现出强烈的____态度。
positive:1.hook: But Silverfang's smile held a secret the contract never mentioned.
positive:1.line: 'I'm *positive* this route leads straight to the Crystal Shelf.'

economic:1.en: At the harbour bazaar, barrels of starfruit and spice crowded every stall. Bell whispered that the island's *economic* heart beat right here, where traders swapped goods for glowing map-shards. Old Helm listened, eyes moving from booth to booth, counting something only he could see.
economic:1.cnHint: 小铃向大家解释这个集市是整座岛屿____活动的核心。
economic:1.hook: One stall, however, sold nothing — and its owner watched us too closely.
economic:1.line: 'The *economic* heart of this island beats right here in the bazaar.'

link:1.en: A chain of lanterns ran from post to post along the bridge road, each one a warm gold circle. Bell pointed out that every lantern was a *link* in a message-line stretching across three islands, carrying news by flashes of light. Old Helm nodded slowly, already reading its signals.
link:1.cnHint: 小铃指出每盏灯笼都是跨越三座岛屿消息传递链条中的一个____。
link:1.hook: The next flash came too soon, and its pattern meant danger.
link:1.line: 'Each lantern is a *link* in the message-line crossing these islands.'

produce:1.en: In the terraced gardens above the market, workers harvested clouds of silver moss that could *produce* a faint, steady light when dried. Silverfang strolled past with both hands behind his back, pretending not to notice, yet his eyes missed nothing. The troupe followed at a careful distance.
produce:1.cnHint: 梯田花园里的工人们采收一种干燥后能____微光的银色苔藓。
produce:1.hook: Silverfang already knew a use for that light we had not imagined.
produce:1.line: 'This dried moss can *produce* a steady glow through the longest night.'

teach:1.en: An old woman sat on a stone step by the crossroads, drawing star-charts in chalk. She offered to *teach* anyone who stopped the names of islands too small for any official map. Bell crouched down at once, eyes wide. Old Helm paid the woman a handful of bright tokens.
teach:1.cnHint: 十字路口一位老妇人主动提出要____路人那些小岛的名字。
teach:1.hook: One tiny island on her chart had no name — only a warning sign.
teach:1.line: 'I will *teach* you the names of every island the big maps forget.'

worth:1.en: Silverfang held up a small compass carved from black stone. 'Not *worth* much to most,' he said at the open-air auction, voice smooth as still water. Yet every captain in the crowd leaned forward. Old Helm crossed his arms; he alone knew what the compass actually pointed to.
worth:1.cnHint: 银牙在露天拍卖会上展示一枚黑石罗盘，声称它并不____多少钱。
worth:1.hook: The bidding stopped — and then one gloved hand rose from the back.
worth:1.line: 'Not *worth* much to most, but priceless to those who know.'

common:1.en: The cobbled street outside the waystation was busy with a mix of traders, flyers, and wandering cloud-herders. Bell said sky travel had become so *common* here that even children rode small personal gliders to school. Old Helm smiled at that, watching a glider skim the rooftops like a bright leaf.
common:1.cnHint: 小铃说在这里，天空旅行已经变得非常____，连孩子们都骑滑翔机上学。
common:1.hook: Then one glider veered off course and dropped toward the crowd.
common:1.line: 'Sky travel is so *common* here that even children glide to school.'

daily:1.en: Every morning on Terrace Row, the island's pilots gathered for a *daily* weather reading, tapping glass instruments and checking wind-threads tied to iron poles. I joined the edge of the group, notebook open. Bell stood beside me, quietly naming each tool and what it measured.
daily:1.cnHint: 露台街上的飞行员们每天举行____气象读数仪式，小铃在旁边为我一一讲解。
daily:1.hook: Today's reading showed a storm that the instruments had never seen before.
daily:1.line: 'This *daily* reading tells us whether the sky will be kind or cruel.'

policy:1.en: Silverfang's crew had posted a notice on the harbour board of the first floating island. Their *policy* was clear: any troupe wishing to cross their sky-bridge must hand over one word-fragment first. Old Helm read it twice, jaw tight. I watched the bridge sway in the wind and wondered if we had anything worth trading.
policy:1.cnHint: 竞争船长的船队在港口公告栏贴出了一条规定，想过天桥的队伍必须先交出一张词语碎片，老舵主看完后神情凝重，我们该怎么办呢？
policy:1.hook: The bridge swayed, and our only fragment trembled in Old Helm's hand.
policy:1.line: 'Our *policy* is simple: pay the toll, or turn back.'

industry:1.en: The second floating island was loud with hammering and smoke. Every corner of it buzzed with *industry*: workers shaped sky-metal into ship parts, traders called out prices, and sparks flew like tiny stars. Bell pulled me close and whispered that Silverfang bought his fastest engines here. I felt a cold feeling rise in my chest.
industry:1.cnHint: 第二座浮岛到处是热火朝天的生产景象，小铃悄悄告诉我，竞争船长的快速引擎就是在这里购买的。
industry:1.hook: Somewhere in that smoke, Silverfang's crew was already one step ahead.
industry:1.line: 'This whole island runs on *industry* — and Silverfang funds half of it.'

concern:1.en: Old Helm gathered us near the market fountain before we moved on. His face showed quiet *concern* as he unrolled our map and pointed to a gap where two fragments were still missing. 'We are behind,' he said softly. Bell nodded without a word. Even the fountain seemed to murmur in agreement.
concern:1.cnHint: 老舵主在市场喷泉旁展开地图，指着两处空缺，神情里透出深深的____。
concern:1.hook: Two fragments missing — and Silverfang's ship had just left the dock.
concern:1.line: 'My *concern* is not the race — it is what we lose if we rush.'

present:1.en: A small child near the island gate held out a folded paper to me. It was a *present*, she said — a drawing of our troupe's flag she had spotted from her window. I took it with both hands. Old Helm smiled, the first real smile I had seen from him all morning. Small gifts land the hardest.
present:1.cnHint: 岛门旁一个小女孩把一幅手绘图递给我，说这是送给我们的____，老舵主见状露出了今天第一个真心的笑容。
present:1.hook: Tucked inside the drawing was a corner torn from a word-fragment map.
present:1.line: 'This *present* is small, but it comes from a good heart.'

claim:1.en: Silverfang appeared at the edge of the market square, arms folded, chin high. He looked at our newly found fragment and began to *claim* it had been stolen from his chest the night before. A crowd gathered quickly. Bell stepped forward, calm as still water, and asked him to prove it. He could not.
claim:1.cnHint: 竞争船长突然出现在广场边缘，____我们刚找到的词语碎片是他的，小铃镇定地要求他拿出证据。
claim:1.hook: Silverfang's eyes narrowed — this was far from over.
claim:1.line: 'I *claim* that fragment, and everyone here will hear why.'

half:1.en: The bet was struck in the open square at noon. Old Helm and Silverfang would each race to reach the next island's crystal tower. The loser would hand over *half* of their word-fragments. Bell drew a starting line in the dust with her boot. I held my breath as both captains turned to face the horizon.
half:1.cnHint: 老舵主和竞争船长在广场当众打赌，输的一方要交出____的词语碎片，小铃用靴子在地上画出了起跑线。
