half:1.hook: The dust settled — and neither captain looked willing to lose.
half:1.line: 'Lose this, and we give up *half* of everything we have found.'

successful:1.en: Old Helm returned to the square before the sun had moved far. He was breathing hard but his eyes were bright. The crowd parted for him. Bell checked the tower token in his hand and gave a single nod: he had made it. A *successful* run against the fastest captain on the sky-roads was no small thing.
successful:1.cnHint: 老舵主气喘吁吁地回到广场，小铃查验了他手中的塔牌后点了点头，他的这次赌赛是____的。
successful:1.hook: Silverfang arrived moments later, silent and pale with fury.
successful:1.line: 'A *successful* captain knows when to be bold and when to be still.'

access:1.en: With Silverfang's fragments added to our own, Bell could finally open the sealed gate at the island's far end. The word carved above it glowed as she pressed the combined map to the lock. *Access* to the next sky-road was ours at last. The gate swung wide, and a warm wind full of star-light rushed in to greet us.
access:1.cnHint: 小铃将合并后的地图碎片按在封印大门的锁上，我们终于获得了前往下一条天路的____，大门缓缓打开。
access:1.hook: Beyond the gate, a new island drifted into view — and it was enormous.
access:1.line: 'We have *access* now — let us not waste a single moment of it.'

fruit:0.en: Inside the trading post, jars of every colour lined the shelves. Old Helm lifted one and turned it slowly in the lamplight. 'Each island grows something different,' he said. The jar held a single preserved *fruit*, strange and golden, the kind that only grew on islands no map had ever named. I understood then — tasting new places was the whole point.
fruit:0.cnHint: 老船长向我展示了一只装着珍贵____的罐子，说明了收集地图碎片的真正意义。
fruit:0.hook: The label on the jar named an island none of us had ever heard of.
fruit:0.line: 'Every *fruit* we find is proof the island was real,' Old Helm said.

waste:0.en: Silverfang spread the star-charts across the low table and tapped one square of blank parchment. 'A whole week drifting near that cloud-bank,' he muttered, 'and nothing.' Bell looked up quietly. 'Then we learned where the words are not.' Silverfang almost smiled. I realized then that even a wrong turn was not a true *waste* if you remembered what you found.
waste:0.cnHint: 银牙为一段没有收获的航行懊恼，但领航员让他明白那段时间并没有____。
waste:0.hook: Bell folded the blank square and slipped it into her coat like a prize.
waste:0.line: 'I refuse to *waste* another night on a cloud-bank with no words,' Silverfang said.

learning:0.en: The trading post kept a small back room full of notes left by other travellers. Old Helm called it the Wall of Voices. I spent an hour reading every scrap. 'This is how we do it,' he said from the doorway. 'Every troupe adds to it.' All that shared *learning* hung on rough wooden boards — and somewhere in those notes, I was sure, was the next island's name.
learning:0.cnHint: 老船长带我参观了一间堆满旅行者笔记的小屋，那里存放着无数前人留下的____。
learning:0.hook: One note ended mid-sentence, as if the writer had run out into the night.
learning:0.line: 'The *learning* on these walls is worth more than any single map,' Old Helm said.

manager:0.en: The trading post was run by a quiet woman who knew every traveller by the word they last collected. Silverfang called her the *manager* of memories, though she just called herself the keeper. She slid a small wooden tile across the counter without being asked. 'You look like someone who just joined a troupe,' she said. The tile had a single island name carved into it.
manager:0.cnHint: 交易站的____悄悄递给我一块木牌，上面刻着一个从未见过的岛屿名称。
manager:0.hook: She had already turned away before I could ask how she knew.
manager:0.line: 'Every *manager* of this post adds one word to the wall before they leave,' she said.

knowledge:0.en: Bell laid three star-charts side by side and pointed to a gap where no island was drawn. 'Most navigators avoid that gap,' she said. 'They think it is empty.' She tapped her temple. '*Knowledge* like that — knowing where everyone else is afraid to look — is the only compass worth carrying.' I leaned in closer. The gap between the charts looked, suddenly, like an open door.
knowledge:0.cnHint: 领航员向我解释，了解其他人不敢探索之地，才是最有价值的____。
knowledge:0.hook: In the gap between the charts, a very faint star had been pencilled in.
knowledge:0.line: '*Knowledge* of the blank spaces is rarer than knowledge of the islands,' Bell said.

mental:0.en: After three days of decoding old word-tiles, my head felt full of fog. Old Helm set a warm drink in front of me and sat down. 'The hardest part of this work is not the sailing,' he said. 'It is the *mental* effort of holding ten possible routes at once and choosing none until the right one appears.' I wrapped both hands around the cup and felt, slowly, the fog begin to lift.
mental:0.cnHint: 老船长告诉我，这份工作最艰难的部分其实是____上的消耗，而非体力上的疲惫。
mental:0.hook: He pushed a single new tile across the table — one route, already chosen.
mental:0.line: 'The *mental* work is what separates a good troupe from a lucky one,' Old Helm said.

weight:0.en: Silverfang dropped his pack onto the trading-post floor with a heavy thud. Inside were seventeen word-tiles, each carved from stone unique to its island. Bell raised an eyebrow. 'You carry the *weight* of every place we have ever been,' she said. He shrugged, but I saw the small satisfied look on his face. Those stones were not a burden — they were a collection of doors he refused to leave behind.
weight:0.cnHint: 银牙随身携带着每一块沉重的石制词牌，领航员说那是他一路走来所有地方的____。
weight:0.hook: One tile at the bottom of the pack glowed faintly in the lamplight.
weight:0.line: 'I know the *weight* — I chose to carry it,' Silverfang said.

academic:0.en: A young traveller at the next table was reading a thick book and taking careful notes. 'He studies the islands without ever visiting them,' Silverfang said, low and flat. Old Helm shook his head gently. 'There is real value in *academic* work — he may know something our boots never taught us.' I glanced at the young traveller's notes and spotted, near the bottom of one page, a word I had never seen before.
academic:0.cnHint: 老船长认为那位只做____研究、从不出海的旅行者，或许掌握着我们实地探索所学不到的知识。
academic:0.hook: The word on his page matched the blank space on our newest chart.
academic:0.line: 'Never look down on *academic* knowledge — it has saved voyages before,' Old Helm said.

determine:1.en: Silverfang spread a betting chart across a barrel on the sky-dock. Old Helm studied every column, his finger tracing routes between three rival islands. He needed to *determine* which passage would cost our troupe the fewest coins before sunrise, or Silverfang's wager would swallow our whole season's earnings.
determine:1.cnHint: 老舵长必须____出哪条航路花费最少，否则就会输掉整季的收入。
determine:1.hook: The sun was already climbing, and Old Helm had not moved.
determine:1.line: 'I must *determine* the safest route before you collect a single coin from us.'

response:1.en: Silverfang called out across the dock in a loud, clear voice, offering any traveller a free passage in exchange for one rare word-fragment. The crowd went quiet. Then, from behind a stack of rope coils, Bell stepped forward. Her calm *response* surprised every sailor on the platform.
response:1.cnHint: 银牙向人群喊话，而贝尔沉静的____让所有水手都愣住了。
response:1.hook: No one had expected the navigator to speak at all.
response:1.line: 'Her *response* was the bravest thing I heard all morning,' Old Helm said softly.

search:1.en: We spread out across the open market on the lower dock, moving between stalls of glowing stones and bottled wind. Our *search* for the missing word-fragment had already taken half the morning. Bell kept her map raised, turning it slowly, hoping some shape in the crowd would match its outline.
search:1.cnHint: 我们在集市上展开____，贝尔举着地图，希望找到失落的词语碎片。
search:1.hook: Then a child tugged Bell's sleeve and pointed upward.
search:1.line: 'Our *search* ends here — the fragment has to be somewhere on this dock.'

due:1.en: Old Helm counted out the coins he owed Silverfang, stacking them neatly on the barrel. The debt was *due* at midday, and the sun was already high. I watched his hands — steady, unhurried — as if paying a rival captain were no different from buying bread at any ordinary market.
due:1.cnHint: 老舵长在正午前必须还清____的欠款，他沉稳地将硬币摆好。
due:1.hook: Silverfang smiled, but his eyes were counting something else entirely.
due:1.line: 'The amount is *due* now — count it yourself if you do not trust my hands.'

regard:1.en: The dock hands stepped aside as Old Helm walked through. Every sailor along the platform seemed to *regard* him with a mixture of respect and quiet worry. Silverfang noticed it too, and for a moment his confident expression faltered, like a sail losing its wind over open sky.
regard:1.cnHint: 码头上的水手们用某种复杂的眼神____着老舵长，这让银牙的自信微微动摇。
regard:1.hook: Even a rival captain cannot ignore what a whole dock feels.
regard:1.line: 'I *regard* Old Helm as the finest navigator these skies have ever carried.'

true:1.en: Silverfang leaned close and said our troupe's map was a copy, not the original. Bell said nothing at first. Then she unfolded the oldest layer and showed him a detail no copy could hold. The mark was *true* — an original seal pressed into the paper long before either of them was born.
true:1.cnHint: 银牙质疑地图的真假，贝尔展开最古老的一层，证明它是____的原版。
true:1.hook: Silverfang's hand reached out, then slowly pulled back.
true:1.line: 'Every mark on this map is *true* — I staked my compass on it.'

depend:1.en: Old Helm turned to the troupe and said nothing for a long moment. Then he explained that whether we kept our vessel or handed it over to Silverfang would *depend* entirely on what word-fragment Bell found before the third bell rang from the harbour tower above us.
depend:1.cnHint: 老舵长说，船队的命运____贝尔能否在第三声钟响前找到词语碎片。
depend:1.hook: The harbour tower bell rang once, then fell silent.
depend:1.line: 'Everything we have built together will *depend* on the next few minutes.'

expensive:1.en: Silverfang gestured to his vessel — a long, polished sky-craft with brass fittings that caught the starlight even in full morning sun. He said it was the most *expensive* ship on the floating docks, worth more than a hundred word-fragments. He offered to wager it, smiling as if he had already won.
expensive:1.cnHint: 银牙指着自己那艘华丽的船，说它是浮空码头上最____的飞船，并把它押作赌注。
expensive:1.hook: Old Helm looked at the ship, then looked away too quickly.
expensive:1.line: 'It is *expensive*, yes — but a ship without a good crew is only a beautiful cage.'

explain:1.en: On the open deck of our sky-ship, Silverfang crossed his arms and waited. Old Helm had promised to share the route, but he had not said a single word for an hour. 'You owe us a reason,' Bell said quietly. Old Helm finally turned and began to *explain* the strange ink marks on the map.
explain:1.cnHint: 老舵手终于开口，用地图上的奇怪符号____了他沉默一小时的原因。
explain:1.hook: But one mark on the map had no name at all.
explain:1.line: 'Allow me to *explain* why we must never cross the red line.'

examine:1.en: Bell knelt at the edge of the landing stone and peered down. The surface was covered in tiny symbols none of us had seen before. She pulled out her lens and began to *examine* each mark with slow, careful movements, as if the stone might answer her if she was patient enough.
examine:1.cnHint: 小铃用放大镜仔细____落脚石上那些从未见过的奇怪符号。
examine:1.hook: The last symbol shifted the moment she touched it.
examine:1.line: 'Let me *examine* this mark before we take another step.'

influence:1.en: Silverfang stood at the crossroads of two sky-paths and said that wind alone decides which way a troupe should sail. Old Helm shook his head. He believed that the words we carry *influence* our course just as much as any wind, pulling the ship toward places that need to be named.
influence:1.cnHint: 老舵手认为，我们收集的词语会____航行的方向，就像风一样。
influence:1.hook: Silverfang smiled, and that smile felt like a dare.
influence:1.line: 'Those old words still *influence* the currents beneath us.'

argue:1.en: Two island merchants blocked the narrow bridge, each holding a different coloured lantern. They began to *argue* about which light was bright enough to guide travellers safely across. Voices rose. Bell stepped between them, lifted both lanterns at once, and said that together the two lights made a perfect path.
argue:1.cnHint: 两位岛上商人为哪盏灯更亮而激烈____，小铃巧妙地化解了僵局。
argue:1.hook: The bridge creaked, reminding everyone it would not wait forever.
argue:1.line: 'It is pointless to *argue* when the storm is already here.'

pass:1.en: Our ship drifted toward a narrow gap between two great rocks. Old Helm held the wheel steady. Everyone watched in silence. We began to *pass* through the gap so slowly that I could reach out and feel the cold stone on either side. Then open sky opened ahead like a held breath released.
pass:1.cnHint: 船慢慢____两块巨岩之间的缝隙，所有人屏气凝神。
pass:1.hook: Something carved into the rock caught my eye just too late.
pass:1.line: 'We will *pass* this point only if we trust the current.'

serious:1.en: Silverfang landed his small craft beside ours without warning and jumped aboard wearing a wide grin. But his eyes were different — still and dark. Old Helm looked at him for a long moment. 'You are *serious* this time,' Old Helm said. It was not a question. Silverfang set a sealed envelope on the table.
serious:1.cnHint: 老舵手一眼看穿竞争船长这次是____的，不是来开玩笑的。
serious:1.hook: Inside the envelope was a map none of us had drawn.
serious:1.line: 'I am completely *serious*; this bet will decide the next route.'

despite:1.en: Rain had been falling for two hours and the viewing platform was soaked. *Despite* the wet, a small crowd had gathered to watch Old Helm read the new word aloud. When he spoke it, a faint circle of light bloomed in the clouds above us, marking the outline of an island no one had recorded.
despite:1.cnHint: ____大雨，人们仍聚在观景台上，见证新词语点亮了天空中的轮廓。
despite:1.hook: The light faded before anyone could trace the island's shape.
despite:1.line: '*Despite* the fog, I can still see where we need to go.'

express:1.en: Bell stood at the prow and looked at the horizon for a long time after Silverfang's bet was made. She is not one to speak quickly. When she finally turned to face us, she chose each word with care to *express* exactly how much danger she thought the wager held. Even Old Helm listened without interrupting.
express:1.cnHint: 小铃字斟句酌，____了她对这场赌约究竟有多危险的判断。
express:1.hook: When she finished, the whole deck stayed perfectly quiet.
express:1.line: 'I want to *express* one clear warning before we agree to this.'

conduct:1.en: On the stone bridge above the market square, Silverfang walked with slow, deliberate steps. Old Helm watched from the far rail, arms folded. 'The crowd is judging us,' Bell whispered. Our *conduct* here would mark us as trustworthy traders or common wanderers for the rest of the journey.
conduct:1.cnHint: 银牙在市场石桥上走得很慢，老舵明白，众人正在观察我们的____。
conduct:1.hook: One wrong move, and the bridge gate would never open.
conduct:1.line: 'Our *conduct* on this bridge decides whether they trust us.'

reveal:1.en: Bell pressed her hand against the stone arch, and a soft blue light began to spread across the carvings. Slowly the arch began to *reveal* a hidden map of the next island, etched deep in the rock. Old Helm leaned close, his eyes wide with quiet joy.
reveal:1.cnHint: 贝尔触摸石拱门，它慢慢____了下一座岛屿的隐藏地图。
reveal:1.hook: But the last corner of the map was already fading fast.
reveal:1.line: 'Watch — the stone will *reveal* the path if you trust it.'

powerful:1.en: A sudden wind swept across the open courtyard, scattering our map fragments like dry leaves. Silverfang stood firm, feet wide apart, both arms out. 'He looks *powerful* standing there,' Bell said softly. Old Helm only smiled. 'He is — but so is the wind. Collect every piece.'
powerful:1.cnHint: 一阵强风吹散了地图碎片，银牙____地站在庭院中央试图拦住它们。
powerful:1.hook: The last fragment spun toward the edge of the floating island.
powerful:1.line: 'Stand *powerful* or the wind takes everything we earned today.'

push:1.en: The old market gate had not moved in years. Old Helm studied it, then turned to us. 'One clean *push* — all together.' We lined up, shoulders touching. The gate groaned, shifted, and swung wide, flooding the narrow street with golden morning light and the smell of distant rain.
push:1.cnHint: 老舵带领大家齐力一____，终于推开了多年未动的古老市门。
push:1.hook: Beyond the gate, something hummed — low, steady, alive.
push:1.line: 'One firm *push* together, and this old gate will answer us.'

wonder:1.en: We stepped off the rope bridge onto a platform of pale white stone. Below us, clouds drifted in slow circles. Bell spun around, arms open. The sight filled me with quiet *wonder* — I had never stood above the clouds before. Old Helm touched my shoulder. 'Welcome to the upper roads.'
wonder:1.cnHint: 踏上云端石台，我满心____，从未想到自己会站在云朵之上。
wonder:1.hook: Then the platform trembled, just once, beneath our feet.
wonder:1.line: 'Let the *wonder* settle — then we move, eyes sharp.'

design:1.en: Silverfang unrolled a rough sketch on the market table. 'I *design* every route myself,' he said, tracing the lines with one finger. 'No shortcut, no wasted step.' Old Helm studied it in silence, then gave a slow nod. Bell was already copying the key details into her small notebook.
design:1.cnHint: 银牙在市场桌上铺开草图，自称亲自____每一条航线，绝不浪费一步。
design:1.hook: Old Helm's nod hid something — a detail only he had noticed.
design:1.line: 'I *design* every course myself — trust the lines, not luck.'

exercise:1.en: Every dawn Bell would *exercise* on the wide steps of the harbour square — ten slow stretches, then a quick run to the far lamp post and back. 'Navigation is half body, half mind,' she told me, not even short of breath. I started joining her on the third morning.
exercise:1.cnHint: 贝尔每天清晨都在港口广场台阶上____，她说领航需要强健的身体和清醒的头脑。
exercise:1.hook: On the fourth morning, she handed me a spare map to carry.
exercise:1.line: '*Exercise* every dawn — a sharp body keeps the route clear.'

space:1.en: The floating market was crowded, stalls pressed together with barely room to breathe. Old Helm found a quiet *space* between two empty carts and spread our word-map flat on the ground. 'Here,' he said. 'We plan here, away from ears.' Silverfang arrived a moment later, glancing back over his shoulder.
space:1.cnHint: 老舵在两辆空车之间找到一块____，把地图铺开，远离嘈杂的人群悄悄商议。
space:1.hook: Silverfang's backward glance meant someone had followed us here.
space:1.line: 'This *space* between the carts — small, but enough for the truth.'

real:1.en: The morning market on Saltbridge Island buzzed with colour. Merchants called out prices, and strange smells filled the air. Old Helm stopped at a stall selling glowing map pieces. 'These look pretty,' he said, 'but are they *real*?' The seller smiled too quickly, and I felt a cold doubt settle in my chest.
real:1.cnHint: 老舵在市集上看到发光的地图碎片，却怀疑它们是否____。
real:1.hook: The seller's hand moved toward the back curtain.
real:1.line: 'Tell me honestly — is this *real* or just a pretty trick?'

talk:1.en: Outside the harbour gate, Silverfang leaned against a post, arms crossed. Old Helm walked straight up to him. The two captains stood close, voices low. I could not hear the words, but the *talk* was clearly serious — Bell grabbed my sleeve and whispered, 'Do not interrupt them. Not now.'
talk:1.cnHint: 银牙和老舵在港口外低声____，贝尔拦住了我。
talk:1.hook: Then Silverfang laughed, and the sound was not friendly.
talk:1.line: 'This *talk* is between captains. Step back, newcomer.'

energy:1.en: The wind turbines of Gustmill Island spun fast overhead, filling the sky with a steady hum. Bell explained that the island stored its *energy* in giant blue crystals along the ridge. Old Helm pressed a hand to one crystal and smiled. 'Enough power here to fly us three islands further,' he said.
energy:1.cnHint: 贝尔介绍风车岛把____储存在山脊的蓝色水晶里。
energy:1.hook: One crystal had a crack running straight through its centre.
energy:1.line: 'All this *energy*, and we have not claimed a single crystal yet.'

plan:1.en: We spread the map across a flat rock near the crossroads. Old Helm traced a route with his finger while Bell counted the remaining word-fragments. 'Three words left, three islands ahead,' she said. Old Helm nodded. 'Then the *plan* is simple: collect, move, climb.' Silverfang's shadow fell across the map before we could roll it up.
plan:1.cnHint: 老舵在路口石头上摊开地图，说明接下来的____。
plan:1.hook: Silverfang had read every word of the route.
plan:1.line: 'Your *plan* is simple. Mine is better. Care to bet?'

bear:1.en: The old rope bridge swayed over the fog below. Bell tested the first plank with her boot. 'I am not sure it can *bear* all three of us,' she said quietly. Old Helm went first, arms out for balance. The wood creaked but held. I followed, eyes fixed on his back, trying not to look down.
bear:1.cnHint: 贝尔担心旧桥能否____三个人的重量。
bear:1.hook: Halfway across, one plank split with a sharp crack.
bear:1.line: 'The bridge must *bear* our weight — there is no other way over.'

organization:1.en: A noticeboard near the dockside was covered in bright posters. One caught my eye: a group called the Sky Keepers, an *organization* that recorded every floating island ever found. Old Helm read it over my shoulder. 'They have been mapping longer than we have,' he said, sounding both impressed and a little worried.
organization:1.cnHint: 码头布告栏上有一个专门记录浮岛的____的海报。
organization:1.hook: The poster listed our troupe's name under 'vessels of interest.'
organization:1.line: 'That *organization* knows things about these islands we do not.'

opportunity:1.en: Silverfang's ship was docked just ahead of ours, its crew busy loading crates. Old Helm watched them carefully. 'They are heading to the Crystal Shelf,' he murmured. Bell's eyes lit up. 'Then this is our *opportunity* to reach it first.' She was already untying the ropes before Old Helm could agree or object.
opportunity:1.cnHint: 看到银牙的船队出发，贝尔觉得这是抢先到达水晶礁的____。
opportunity:1.hook: Silverfang turned and looked directly at Bell.
opportunity:1.line: 'Every *opportunity* has a cost — do not forget who taught you that.'

professor:1.en: Near the open-air lecture steps, an elderly woman with star-charts pinned to her coat was speaking to a small crowd. Old Helm bowed his head respectfully. 'She is the *professor* who first proved the islands move with the seasons,' he whispered. She paused mid-sentence, looked straight at me, and said, 'You. Come here.'
professor:1.cnHint: 一位研究浮岛运动规律的____在露天台阶上演讲，突然叫住了我。
professor:1.hook: She held out a chart covered in marks I could not read.
professor:1.line: 'The *professor* never wastes words — if she calls you, listen.'

career:1.en: Silverfang leaned against a lamp post at the edge of Market Deck, arms crossed. 'Every stop on this route is part of my *career*,' he said, sweeping a hand toward the glowing stalls below. Old Helm just smiled. Bell added the word to our map, and a new island shimmered into view on the horizon.
career:1.cnHint: 银牙向我们解释，每一次停靠都是他____的一部分，老掌舵人只是微笑以对。
career:1.hook: But why did Silverfang's eyes flick to the locked chest behind him?
career:1.line: 'Every port I visit is a chapter in my *career*.'

medium:1.en: The island market sold all kinds of things, but the strangest stall offered 'words as *medium*' — small glass bottles, each holding a whisper of meaning. Bell picked one up carefully. Old Helm nodded: the right medium could carry a message farther than any ship. I wrote the word down and felt the map pulse warmly in my pocket.
medium:1.cnHint: 市集上有个奇特的摊位，以"词语"作为____来传递信息，贝尔小心地拿起一个瓶子。
medium:1.hook: The bottle in Bell's hand began to glow the moment she spoke.
medium:1.line: 'A good *medium* carries meaning without losing a single word.'

office:1.en: At the heart of Anchor Plaza stood a small wooden *office* — barely bigger than a supply crate — where the island's trade master stamped travel permits. Old Helm handed over our papers without a word. I watched the stamp fall: thud. Bell grinned at me. One stamp, and the next island appeared on our chart like a gift.
office:1.cnHint: 广场中央有一间小小的____，老掌舵人在那里办理了通行手续。
office:1.hook: The trade master whispered a warning before sliding the papers back.
office:1.line: 'Every traveller must pass through my *office* before moving on.'

culture:1.en: The floating market of Windhollow was famous for its *culture* of sharing — every trader offered a free taste before asking for coin. Old Helm said this custom was older than any map we carried. Bell jotted the word beside a sketch of paper lanterns. I tried a warm spiced roll and decided this island was already my favourite.
culture:1.cnHint: 风谷浮岛的____是无偿分享，每位商人都会先赠予，再谈价钱。
culture:1.hook: Then a vendor pressed a sealed letter into Old Helm's hand.
culture:1.line: 'Our *culture* here is simple: share first, trade second.'

college:1.en: Bell pointed to a tall building draped in climbing vines. 'That used to be a *college*,' she said, 'where students came to learn the language of stars.' Old Helm touched the door gently. The wood hummed. I added the word to our map and the door swung open, cool air rushing out like a held breath finally released.
college:1.cnHint: 贝尔指着一栋爬满藤蔓的高楼，说那曾是一所学习星语的____。
college:1.hook: Inside, a single lantern still burned on an empty desk.
college:1.line: 'This *college* taught navigators to read the sky, not just the sea.'

value:1.en: Silverfang spread his goods on a low table and watched us closely. 'Know the *value* of what you carry,' he said, tapping the corner of our word-map, 'or someone else will set the price for you.' Old Helm raised an eyebrow but said nothing. Bell copied the word in careful letters, and a faint new path lit up across the chart.
value:1.cnHint: 银牙提醒我们要清楚自己所携之物的____，否则别人就会替你定价。
value:1.hook: Silverfang smiled, but his hand never left the table.
value:1.line: 'Never trade until you know the *value* of what you hold.'

connection:1.en: The rope bridge between Driftstone and the next island swayed in the wind, each plank worn smooth by years of feet. 'This *connection* is old,' Old Helm said quietly, steadying a rope with both hands. Bell tested her weight on the first plank and nodded back to me. I stepped on, heart light, and the stars seemed to lean in to watch.
connection:1.cnHint: 两座岛屿之间的绳桥是岛民多年来赖以维系的____，老掌舵人轻声说道。
connection:1.hook: Halfway across, one plank cracked loud as a gunshot.
connection:1.line: 'Guard this *connection* — once a bridge is lost, islands forget each other.'

story:1.en: Old Helm sat on an upturned barrel at the edge of the night market and began to speak. Every island, he said, holds a *story* older than its oldest tree, and collecting words was just another way of collecting those stories. The crowd leaned in. Bell caught my eye and smiled. I felt, for the first time, that I truly belonged to this troupe.
story:1.cnHint: 老掌舵人在夜市边讲起每座岛屿都藏着一个古老的____，人群纷纷侧耳倾听。
story:1.hook: Then he paused and looked at me — 'Your turn.'
story:1.line: 'Every word we find is a piece of someone's *story*.'

force:1.en: Old Helm planted his boots on the rope bridge and crossed his arms. Silverfang's crew blocked the far end, demanding the troupe hand over their map fragments. 'No one can *force* us to give up what we earned,' Old Helm said quietly. The wind hummed between the planks.
force:1.cnHint: 银牙的船员堵住桥头，想____我们交出地图碎片。
force:1.hook: One wrong step, and the bridge would not forgive us.
force:1.line: 'No one can *force* us off this bridge, not today.'

importance:1.en: Bell spread the map fragments across a wide stone table at the edge of Cloverfield Market. She traced the connecting lines with her finger, explaining each piece to the troupe. 'The *importance* of keeping them in order cannot be overstated,' she said. Every vendor nearby leaned in to listen.
importance:1.cnHint: 小铃向大家解释保持地图碎片顺序的____。
importance:1.hook: A single fragment, misplaced, could lead us somewhere we could never leave.
importance:1.line: 'The *importance* of this order is something we must never forget.'

sell:1.en: Silverfang set up a bright stall in the floating market and displayed shining copies of false map fragments. Travellers gathered eagerly, coins ready. But the *sell* was a disappointment — up close, every copy was blank. The crowd murmured and drifted away, leaving Silverfang red-faced in the afternoon light.
sell:1.cnHint: 银牙在市场上兜售假地图碎片，但这次____让他很没面子。
sell:1.hook: Somewhere in that crowd, the real fragment was still missing.
sell:1.line: 'That *sell* went worse than I ever imagined,' Silverfang muttered.

replace:1.en: A gust swept across the sky-dock and knocked one of Bell's navigation stones off the railing. It fell into the clouds below without a sound. Bell stared at the empty spot. 'We will need to *replace* it before we reach the next island,' she said, already sorting through her pack.
replace:1.cnHint: 小铃的导航石被风吹落，她说必须____它。
replace:1.hook: Without that stone, the next passage was little more than a guess.
replace:1.line: 'We must *replace* it before the tide of stars shifts tonight.'

approach:1.en: Old Helm gathered the troupe at dawn near the harbour gate. He drew a small circle in the dust with his boot. 'Our *approach* to Silverfang's challenge must be careful and steady,' he said, tapping the circle. 'We think before we move, and we move together.' Everyone nodded.
approach:1.cnHint: 老舵手向大家说明应对银牙挑战的____。
approach:1.hook: Silverfang was already watching us from the far end of the dock.
approach:1.line: 'Our *approach* must be steady — no rushing, no showing fear.'

engage:1.en: The market street buzzed with colour and noise. Bell stopped at a puzzle-seller's cart, drawn in by a spinning wooden map. She chose to *engage* with the challenge, trading a small coin for a turn. Around her, children cheered. Even Old Helm smiled from the shade of a nearby awning.
engage:1.cnHint: 小铃在市集街头决定____一个解谜摊位的挑战。
engage:1.hook: The puzzle's final piece looked exactly like our missing fragment.
engage:1.line: 'Let us *engage* with this puzzle — it may teach us something useful.'

ensure:1.en: Before the troupe stepped onto Silverfang's sky-platform for the wager, Bell double-checked every rope and anchor pin. She walked the whole circle twice. 'I want to *ensure* that no one falls because we were careless,' she said firmly, pulling the last knot tight as the platform swayed gently.
ensure:1.cnHint: 小铃仔细检查所有绳索，要____大家的安全。
ensure:1.hook: Silverfang watched her work, and for once said nothing at all.
ensure:1.line: 'I will *ensure* every rope holds before any of us takes a step.'

limit:1.en: Silverfang announced the rules of the wager at the top of Windspire Hill, where three islands almost touched. Each side had one hour and one question only. 'There is a *limit* to how much we can argue,' Old Helm told the troupe. 'So let us make our one question count.'
limit:1.cnHint: 老舵手提醒大家，争论是有____的，要把握好唯一的提问机会。
limit:1.hook: The hour glass Silverfang flipped was already running.
limit:1.line: 'There is a *limit* here, so choose our one question with great care.'

perhaps:1.en: The market on Thistledown Island smelled of spice and old rope. Old Helm spread a torn map across a barrel and tapped a blank space near the edge. '*Perhaps* this gap holds the word we need,' he said quietly. The crowd moved around us like water around stone.
perhaps:1.cnHint: 老舵手在市集的木桶上摊开地图，指着一片空白说____这里藏着我们要找的词。
perhaps:1.hook: The blank space on the map began to glow faintly.
perhaps:1.line: '*Perhaps* the missing word is closer than we think.'

video:1.en: A street performer on Coppervane Bridge had set up a small screen showing a *video* of the last known floating island before it vanished into the clouds. Bell leaned close, studying every detail. The images flickered in the wind, but the island's shape was unmistakable.
video:1.cnHint: 一位街头艺人播放着一段关于消失岛屿的____，领航员仔细盯着画面。
video:1.hook: Bell pointed at the corner of the screen and whispered one word.
video:1.line: 'This *video* shows the exact shape of the island we need.'

prevent:1.en: A locked iron gate blocked the entrance to Windshard Alley. A sign said that falling tiles had forced the city guard to *prevent* anyone from passing through. Old Helm folded his arms. The alley was our only shortcut to the word market before it closed at dusk.
prevent:1.cnHint: 铁门和告示牌____所有人进入小巷，但那是通往词语市场的唯一捷径。
prevent:1.hook: Old Helm smiled and reached for something in his coat.
prevent:1.line: 'Nothing can *prevent* us from reaching that market tonight.'

source:1.en: Bell traced the little river on the map all the way to its *source*: a spring hidden beneath the roots of the Great Anchor Tree. 'Every word on this island flows from there,' she said. Old Helm nodded slowly. We packed our bags and turned toward the hills.
source:1.cnHint: 领航员在地图上顺着小河找到了____，据说岛上所有词语都从那里流出。
source:1.hook: Something beneath the Anchor Tree was already singing.
source:1.line: 'The *source* of all the island words lies under that tree.'

available:1.en: The word-market stalls were nearly bare by the time we arrived. Only a few fragments were still *available*, laid out on a faded cloth. A thin merchant spread his hands as if to apologise. Old Helm picked up the smallest fragment and held it to the light with great care.
available:1.cnHint: 抵达词语市场时大多数摊位已空，仅剩几片碎片____，老舵手拿起最小的一片仔细端详。
available:1.hook: That tiny fragment fit perfectly into the blank on our map.
available:1.line: 'Only one fragment is still *available*, and we must take it.'

customer:1.en: Silverfang leaned against a lamp post outside the map-seller's stall, watching every *customer* who came and went. She was looking for someone carrying a blue satchel. Bell noticed her first and tugged my sleeve. Whatever Silverfang was after, she had not come to browse.
customer:1.cnHint: 银牙守在地图摊外，观察着每一位____，她似乎在等一个背蓝色包的人。
customer:1.hook: Then a figure in a blue coat turned the corner.
customer:1.line: 'Every *customer* here is hiding something worth watching.'

language:1.en: The old signboard above the gate was carved in a *language* none of us could read. Bell ran her finger along each symbol slowly. Old Helm said the symbols looked like the ones found on the very first map fragment, the one that had brought us to these islands at all.
language:1.cnHint: 大门上方的木牌刻着一种没人认识的____，领航员和老舵手都觉得它和第一张地图碎片有关联。
language:1.hook: One symbol on the board matched the mark on our compass.
language:1.line: 'This *language* is the same one written on our first map.'

test:1.en: Silverfang stepped forward and blocked our path near the bridge toll post. She set a small jar on the stone railing and crossed her arms. 'A *test*,' she said. 'Name the island written on this jar, and I will give you the route north.' Old Helm narrowed his eyes and studied the jar.
test:1.cnHint: 银牙拦住去路，在护栏上放了一个小罐子，说这是一场____，答对才告诉我们北行路线。
test:1.hook: Old Helm's lips moved silently, reading something none of us saw.
test:1.line: 'This *test* will decide who truly leads the way north.'

save:1.en: On the market bridge, Old Helm spotted a coin rolling toward the edge. He caught it with two fingers and dropped it into a small jar at his belt. 'Every copper we *save* today becomes a sail-patch tomorrow,' he said. The troupe nodded, eyes on the next island's outline.
save:1.cnHint: 老舵主在集市桥上捡起一枚铜币，放入腰间的小罐，说每一枚____下来的铜币都有用处。
save:1.hook: But the jar was already missing from his belt.
save:1.line: 'Every copper we *save* today becomes a sail-patch tomorrow.'

service:1.en: The docking square hummed with traders. Bell stopped at a small stall where an old woman offered map-reading *service* for a handful of seeds. 'She reads the lines better than any compass,' Bell whispered to me. The woman smiled, pressed a dried leaf into my hand, and pointed at the sky.
service:1.cnHint: 贝尔在停靠广场找到一位老妇人，说她提供的____比任何指南针都准。
service:1.hook: The leaf had a path drawn on it — one that led off the edge of every known map.
service:1.line: 'Her map-reading *service* is worth every seed we carry.'

note:1.en: I found a folded paper pinned to the fountain post in the plaza. Inside was a single musical *note* drawn in blue ink, and below it, three words: 'follow the sound.' Old Helm leaned over my shoulder, eyebrows raised. Somewhere above us, a flute began to play that exact note.
note:1.cnHint: 我在广场喷泉柱上发现一张纸，上面只画了一个____，下面写着"跟着声音走"。
note:1.hook: The flute stopped the moment Old Helm reached for the paper.
note:1.line: 'That *note* was left here for someone — and I think it was for us.'

probably:1.en: Silverfang leaned against the harbour gate, arms crossed. 'You are *probably* heading into a wind trap,' he said, watching Old Helm study the cloud shapes. 'I have sailed that corridor twice. Both times I lost cargo.' He smiled anyway, as if the warning were also an invitation to prove him wrong.
probably:1.cnHint: 银牙靠着港口大门，告诉老舵主那条航道____是个风陷阱。
probably:1.hook: Old Helm folded the map and said, 'Third time is different.'
probably:1.line: 'You are *probably* heading into a wind trap — just so you know.'

strategy:1.en: The troupe gathered around a chalk drawing Old Helm had made on the cobblestone. It showed arrows, wind lines, and two island arcs. 'This is our *strategy*,' he said, tapping the centre. 'We move with the morning wind, not against it.' Bell nodded slowly. I copied every arrow into my notebook.
strategy:1.cnHint: 老舵主在石板路上用粉笔画出航行路线，向大家讲解这次的____。
strategy:1.hook: Silverfang's shadow fell across the chalk drawing just then.
strategy:1.line: 'This *strategy* only works if the morning wind holds — let us hope it does.'

building:1.en: At the edge of the floating island stood a tall *building* wrapped in hanging vines, its windows glowing amber. Bell said it was the word-keeper's archive — the place where collected words were turned into real map fragments. We climbed the outside steps slowly, listening to the whole island creak beneath us.
building:1.cnHint: 在浮空岛边缘，有一座爬满藤蔓、窗户发出琥珀光的____，据说是词语保管人的档案馆。
building:1.hook: The door swung open before any of us knocked.
building:1.line: 'That *building* holds more map pieces than we have ever dreamed of finding.'

community:1.en: The lower market was alive with voices. Old Helm explained that every trader here belonged to the same sky-sailing *community*, sharing wind reports and safe routes as freely as bread. 'No one survives these islands alone,' he said. A child ran past and pressed a small star-shaped badge into my palm.
community:1.cnHint: 下层集市的商人们都属于同一个____，像分享面包一样自由交流风向情报。
community:1.hook: The badge was stamped with a route number no chart in our bag had ever listed.
community:1.line: 'In this *community*, you share what you know or you sail alone.'

internet:1.en: Bell pointed to a web of glowing threads stretched between six tall poles in the square — the island's *internet*, she called it, a light-signal network that carried news from island to island in seconds. Old Helm pressed his hand against the nearest pole and felt it hum. 'Someone just sent a warning,' he said quietly.
internet:1.cnHint: 贝尔指着广场上连接六根高杆的发光网络，说这是岛屿间的____，能在瞬间传递消息。
internet:1.hook: The warning was in our troupe's own code.
internet:1.line: 'This *internet* of light carries news faster than any ship alive.'

sign:1.en: The market square of Driftstone Island buzzed with colour. Stalls lined every path, each one hung with a painted board. Bell pointed to a cracked wooden board above the map-seller's stall. 'That *sign* shows a compass rose,' she said. 'Wherever we see one like it, a new word is waiting.' I looked up and felt the adventure truly begin.
sign:1.cnHint: 小铃指着地图摊上方的____，说凡是看到这个图案的地方，都藏着一个新单词。
sign:1.hook: But the compass rose was slowly, silently turning on its own.
sign:1.line: 'That *sign* above the stall — it is the mark of the word-keepers.'

feeling:1.en: Old Helm led us through the crowded stone lanes of Ashveil Market. Spice smoke curled around the lamp-posts. I stopped beside a fountain and pressed my hand to its warm edge. A strange *feeling* rose in my chest — not fear, not joy, but something wide and open, like standing at the edge of the sky. 'You sense it too,' Old Helm said softly.
feeling:1.cnHint: 在集市的喷泉旁，叙述者心中升起一种奇特的____，老舵轻声说他也感受到了。
feeling:1.hook: Beneath the fountain, carved letters were beginning to glow.
feeling:1.line: 'That *feeling* in your chest — it means a word is very close.'

professional:1.en: At the centre of Windhook Bazaar stood a woman repairing sky-compasses with steady, careful hands. Every movement was clean and sure. Old Helm watched her and nodded. 'She is a *professional*,' he said. 'She has done this work so long that the tools trust her fingers.' The woman looked up, smiled, and slid a folded word-fragment across the counter to us.
professional:1.cnHint: 在集市中心，老舵称赞一位修理天空罗盘的女人是真正的____，她随后把一张词语碎片递给了我们。
professional:1.hook: The word on the fragment shimmered and rearranged itself before our eyes.
professional:1.line: 'Only a *professional* like her could read the old sky-charts,' said Old Helm.

behind:1.en: Silverfang's crew set up a stall of bright curiosities at the Cloudfoot Fair. When Old Helm reached the stall, Silverfang was already grinning. 'You are *behind*, old friend,' Silverfang said, tapping a small pile of word-fragments on the counter. 'I collected three this morning while you were still eating breakfast.' Old Helm straightened his coat and calmly placed four fragments on the table.
behind:1.cnHint: 在集市上，银牙嘲笑老舵____他，但老舵不慌不忙地拿出了更多词语碎片。
behind:1.hook: One of those fragments held a map to an island none of them had named yet.
behind:1.line: 'You are *behind* me by three words, and the day is only half done,' Silverfang said.

government:1.en: Bell found an old notice board near the harbour gate of Stormledge Port. Most of the papers were torn, but one flat sheet remained. It bore a stamped seal and careful writing. 'This is from the island *government*,' Bell said, reading aloud. 'They once kept a record of every word-fragment ever found here.' I ran my finger down the list and found a name that matched our next clue.
government:1.cnHint: 小铃在港口布告栏上发现了一张来自岛屿____的旧公告，上面记录着所有曾经被发现的词语碎片。
government:1.hook: The last name on the list was one none of us recognised — except the paper itself seemed to tremble.
government:1.line: 'The island *government* sealed this record a hundred years ago,' Bell read quietly.

growth:1.en: The flower market of Sunperch Island was impossible to ignore. Vines climbed every post, and blossoms spilled out of baskets onto the cobblestones. A gardener handed me a small pot with a single green shoot inside. 'We measure time here by *growth*,' she said. 'This shoot was a seed when the last troupe passed through.' I looked at Old Helm, surprised. He just smiled at the sky.
growth:1.cnHint: Sunperch岛的花卉市场里，一位园丁用植物的____来衡量时间，这让叙述者意识到上一支队伍已经离开很久了。
growth:1.hook: At the bottom of the pot, half-buried in soil, lay a folded word-fragment.
growth:1.line: 'We measure the years by *growth* here — one ring of vines for every season passed.'

negative:1.en: Silverfang spread a handful of word-fragments on a barrel at the edge of the night market. Some glowed softly; one stayed dark and cold to the touch. 'A *negative* fragment,' Bell murmured, turning it over. 'It does not open a new place — it closes a false path, so you do not waste your journey.' Silverfang raised an eyebrow. 'Worth more than gold, then,' he said, and Bell agreed.
negative:1.cnHint: 小铃在夜市上发现了一块____的词语碎片，它不能开启新地点，但能封闭错误的路径。
negative:1.hook: The dark fragment began ticking, faintly, like a clock counting down.
negative:1.line: 'A *negative* fragment is rare — it saves you from roads that lead nowhere,' said Bell.

potential:1.en: Old Helm stopped at a small stall selling blank map-tiles at the edge of Glasswind Market. The young seller could not have been older than sixteen. Old Helm studied the careful lines the child had drawn on each tile and tapped one gently. 'Real *potential* here,' he said to me quietly. 'With the right words, this one could chart islands nobody has found yet.' He bought every tile on the table.
potential:1.cnHint: 老舵在集市上发现了一个少年摊主画的地图片，他悄悄告诉叙述者这孩子有真正的____。
potential:1.hook: One tile had an island on it that was not on any of our existing charts.
potential:1.line: 'I see *potential* in these maps that most collectors would walk straight past,' Old Helm said.

seek:1.en: The market on Driftstone Island smelled of salt and old rope. Silverfang moved through the crowd with sharp eyes, clearly on a mission. 'I *seek* the word-keeper,' he told a vendor without slowing down. Old Helm nudged me and whispered that word-keepers only appeared to those who truly needed them.
seek:1.cnHint: 银牙在热闹的市场上穿行，____着传说中掌管词语的人。
seek:1.hook: The vendor smiled and pointed straight at me.
seek:1.line: 'I *seek* the word-keeper — have you seen one pass through here?'

exist:1.en: High on the Arch of Pale Stone, Bell pressed her hand to a crack in the rock. 'Some say this path no longer *exists*,' she said quietly, 'but the map says otherwise.' Mist curled below us, hiding whatever lay between here and the next island. I decided to trust the map.
exist:1.cnHint: 贝尔站在古老的石拱上，坚信那条据说已不____的路仍在某处。
exist:1.hook: Then, slowly, the mist began to part.
exist:1.line: 'If it *exists* on the map, it exists in the world — we keep moving.'

supply:1.en: Silverfang dropped a heavy bag onto the deck and counted out tins, rope, and small glass bottles. 'Three days of *supply* — no more,' he said, eyeing Old Helm. 'So whatever word you are chasing on Ember Isle, find it fast.' Old Helm just smiled, folded the map, and said nothing.
supply:1.cnHint: 银牙清点完物资，提醒大家三天的____只够用到燃烬岛。
supply:1.hook: Old Helm's smile, I had learned, usually meant trouble.
supply:1.line: 'Three days of *supply* is enough — if we do not get lost again.'

visit:1.en: Our *visit* to the floating night market was meant to be quick, just long enough to trade a word-fragment for fuel. But the lanterns were warm and the soup was hot, and somehow an hour slipped by before Old Helm called us back to the ship with a low whistle.
visit:1.cnHint: 我们对夜市的这次____本该短暂，却在温暖的灯光中流连忘返。
visit:1.hook: Old Helm's whistle came a second time, sharper now.
visit:1.line: 'One short *visit*, that was the deal — back to the ship, both of you.'

worry:1.en: The rope bridge between Twin-Peak Island and the next ridge swayed badly in the wind. I stopped halfway across, hands tight on the rail. Bell looked back at me with calm eyes. 'Your *worry* is fair,' she said, 'but the bridge has held for a hundred years. Keep walking.' I kept walking.
worry:1.cnHint: 我在摇晃的绳桥上停下了脚步，贝尔平静地回应了我的____。
worry:1.hook: Behind us, one plank snapped clean off.
worry:1.line: 'Your *worry* makes sense, but the bridge knows what it is doing — trust it.'

adapt:1.en: The air on Coldveil Island was thin and strange, and after an hour my head ached. Bell handed me a small herb pouch. 'Chew one leaf,' she said. 'Your body will *adapt* faster with it.' Within minutes the ache faded and the world sharpened, as if the island had quietly decided to accept me.
adapt:1.cnHint: 冷幕岛的空气令人不适，贝尔给了我一个草药包帮助我____环境。
adapt:1.hook: Then the island made a sound — low, slow, like breathing.
adapt:1.line: 'Chew one leaf and your body will *adapt* — I promise the headache fades.'

bit:1.en: Old Helm tore a tiny corner from the map and held it to the starlight. 'Just a *bit* of paper,' he said, 'but look.' Where the light hit the torn edge, tiny letters glowed gold — the name of an island none of us had heard of. Silverfang leaned in, suddenly very interested.
bit:1.cnHint: 老舵手从地图上撕下一____纸角，对着星光发现了隐藏的字迹。
bit:1.hook: Silverfang read the name aloud, and the wind changed direction.
bit:1.line: 'Just a *bit* of the map, but it holds more secrets than the whole chart.'

check:1.en: Before we cast off from Ashwharf, Bell walked the length of the hull, knocking softly on each plank. 'I always *check* before open sky,' she said. She stopped near the bow, knocked twice more, then nodded with quiet satisfaction. Whatever she had been listening for, she had not found it.
check:1.cnHint: 贝尔在启航前仔细____船体，确认没有任何隐患。
check:1.hook: Then she found something near the rudder that made her go very still.
check:1.line: 'I *check* every plank before open sky — it is the only rule I never break.'

stick:1.en: The market square on Thorn Isle smelled of pine and fresh bread. Silverfang slapped a hand-drawn map onto the wooden post, and it seemed to *stick* there by its own will. 'Every word we collect adds a piece,' he said. Old Helm nodded, eyes tracing the blank edges still waiting to be filled.
stick:1.cnHint: 银牙把地图贴在木柱上，地图仿佛自己____住了，老舵长盯着那些空白边缘若有所思。
stick:1.hook: One blank corner on the map still pulsed with a faint, unknown glow.
stick:1.line: 'Let it *stick*, and the island will remember us.'

effective:1.en: Bell set up a small wind-reading post at the edge of the cliff market. Three coloured ribbons, nothing more. 'Simple but *effective*,' Old Helm murmured, watching the ribbons tell us exactly which sky-lane to take. Within minutes we had our heading and the troupe moved on with quiet confidence.
effective:1.cnHint: 贝尔用三条彩带做了个测风装置，老舵长说这个办法很____，大家很快确定了航向。
effective:1.hook: The leftmost ribbon suddenly snapped flat, pointing toward uncharted sky.
effective:1.line: 'Three ribbons — *effective* enough to save us an hour.'

fear:1.en: A sudden crack split the stone bridge across the gap between two market stalls. I froze. Old Helm placed a steady hand on my shoulder. 'The *fear* is useful,' he said softly, 'it tells you to look before you step.' I looked, found the safe stones, and crossed with care.
fear:1.cnHint: 石桥裂开了一道缝，老舵长说____是有用的，它提醒你迈步前先看清楚。
fear:1.hook: On the far side, the next word-fragment glimmered just out of reach.
fear:1.line: '*Fear* is just the island asking you to pay attention.'

hit:1.en: Silverfang tossed a bright coin toward the old bell tower at the centre of the floating square. It *hit* the bronze surface with a clear, ringing note that echoed across every stall and rooftop. Heads turned. Old Helm smiled. 'Good,' he said. 'Now they know we are here.'
hit:1.cnHint: 银牙扔出一枚铜币____了钟楼，清脆的回响让广场上所有人都注意到了我们。
hit:1.hook: A hooded figure at the far stall turned slowly and held up a word-fragment.
hit:1.line: '*Hit* it clean and the whole island hears you.'

assume:1.en: I reached for the nearest fruit stall, ready to trade. 'Do not *assume* the price,' Bell said quickly, pulling my arm back with a grin. Each island has its own way, she explained. Here, you offer a story first, then a coin. I put my coin away and told the seller about our journey instead.
assume:1.cnHint: 我想直接付钱买水果，贝尔提醒我不能____这里的规矩和别处一样，得先讲故事才能交换。
assume:1.hook: The seller's eyes lit up and she slid a folded word-fragment across the counter.
assume:1.line: 'Never *assume* an island trades the way the last one did.'

generally:1.en: Old Helm spread the collected word-fragments on a low table outside the tea stall. '*Generally*,' he said, tapping the pattern they formed, 'the words point north when a new island is near.' The troupe leaned in. The fragments did indeed lean north, tilting like compass needles hungry for discovery.
generally:1.cnHint: 老舵长把碎片摆在桌上，说____来说，碎片朝北倾斜就表示附近有新岛屿出现。
generally:1.hook: One fragment alone tilted east, as if hiding a secret of its own.
generally:1.line: '*Generally* the words agree — but watch the one that does not.'

interaction:1.en: At the crossroads stall, two word-fragments lay side by side. When Bell set them close together, a soft hum rose between them. 'That *interaction* tells us they belong to the same island,' she said, delighted. Old Helm sketched their combined shape into the map and a new name appeared in the margin.
interaction:1.cnHint: 贝尔把两枚碎片靠近时，它们之间产生了嗡嗡声，这种____说明它们属于同一座岛。
interaction:1.hook: The new name in the margin slowly rearranged itself into a set of coordinates.
interaction:1.line: 'Feel that hum? The *interaction* means they are kin.'

top:1.en: The tallest spire on Thorn Isle had a viewing platform at its *top*, and someone had pinned a word-fragment to the flag there. Silverfang climbed first, fast and grinning. He held the fragment up against the starlit sky, and for a moment the whole island seemed to breathe with us.
top:1.cnHint: 尖塔顶端挂着一枚碎片，银牙爬到____把它取下，举向满天星光，整座岛仿佛跟我们一起呼吸。
top:1.hook: The fragment caught the starlight and projected a map none of us had ever seen.
top:1.line: 'From the *top* you can see which island wakes up next.'

easily:1.en: The market on Driftstone Island was packed with traders. Old Helm led us through the crowd, reading faces like open books. 'Silverfang could *easily* slip an agent in here,' he murmured, eyes moving left and right. I stayed close, watching every stall we passed.
easily:1.cnHint: 老舵在嘈杂的集市上警告大家，银牙____会在人群中安插眼线。
easily:1.hook: Then one trader smiled at us — just a little too wide.
easily:1.line: 'A spy can *easily* hide behind a friendly face,' Old Helm warned.

protect:1.en: Rain swept across the Windhaven docks. Bell spread her wide coat over the map fragments we had collected, pressing them flat against a crate. 'I need to *protect* these from the wet,' she said firmly. Old Helm nodded, then scanned the foggy water for Silverfang's ship.
protect:1.cnHint: 领航员在码头风雨中竭力____珍贵的地图碎片不被淋湿。
protect:1.hook: A horn sounded out on the fog — low, long, and familiar.
protect:1.line: 'I must *protect* every fragment — each one is a place we have not yet seen,' Bell said.

advantage:1.en: Silverfang's crew reached the ridge first and planted their flag at the top. 'They have the high ground,' Bell said under her breath. Old Helm only smiled. 'Let them enjoy that *advantage*,' he said, 'while we find the door they walked right past.' He pointed to a gap in the rock below.
advantage:1.cnHint: 银牙的船员抢占高地，但老舵认为对方的____未必能帮他们找到真正的出口。
advantage:1.hook: The gap in the rock breathed cold air — and something glowed inside.
advantage:1.line: 'Their *advantage* is real, but a high view does not show what lies beneath,' Old Helm said.

break:1.en: We had been hiking the stone path for two hours when Old Helm raised his hand and stopped. 'We take a *break* here,' he announced, settling onto a flat rock beside a small waterfall. Bell handed out dried fruit from her pack. Somewhere below, we could hear Silverfang's crew still arguing over their route.
break:1.cnHint: 长途跋涉后，老舵宣布在瀑布旁____片刻，而银牙的人还在山下争吵。
break:1.hook: The arguing below went suddenly, completely silent.
break:1.line: 'We take a *break* now — a clear head wins more than tired legs,' Old Helm said.

conclude:1.en: Old Helm studied the two paths ahead: one worn smooth, one covered in fresh moss. He knelt, pressed two fingers to the moss, then stood. 'I *conclude* that no one has come this way in weeks,' he said. Bell marked the worn path on her chart, and we moved on without a word.
conclude:1.cnHint: 老舵仔细观察两条岔路后，从苔藓的痕迹____出哪条路近期无人经过。
conclude:1.hook: Bell's pen stopped halfway through the mark, her eyes wide.
conclude:1.line: 'From this moss alone I can *conclude* which path Silverfang has never tried,' Old Helm said.

figure:1.en: A tall shadow stood at the far end of the floating bridge. Bell squinted into the pale morning light. 'That *figure* — do you know it?' she asked. Old Helm folded his arms. 'Silverfang,' he said quietly. 'Right on time.' I gripped the strap of my pack and stood up straight.
figure:1.cnHint: 晨光中，一个高大的____出现在浮桥尽头，老舵一眼认出了来者。
figure:1.hook: Silverfang lifted one hand — not a threat, but an invitation.
figure:1.line: 'That lone *figure* at the bridge end is exactly who I expected,' Old Helm said.

fit:1.en: Bell handed me a spare navigator's vest from her bag. I slipped it on and was surprised — it seemed made for me. 'Does it *fit*?' she asked with a small smile. 'Perfectly,' I said. Old Helm glanced over. 'Good,' he said. 'You look like someone who belongs on a voyage now.'
fit:1.cnHint: 领航员把备用背心递给我，问穿着是否____，老舵说我终于有了出航者的样子。
fit:1.hook: Just then, Silverfang's ship drifted into view — closer than yesterday.
fit:1.line: 'If it does not *fit* you well, the long climb ahead will make it worse,' Bell said.

particular:1.en: Silverfang arrived at the crossroads and paused, then chose the left path without a glance at the right. Bell turned to us, puzzled. 'Why that *particular* path?' she whispered. Old Helm watched until Silverfang was out of sight, then said softly, 'Because something on it was already moved. Someone told him.'
particular:1.cnHint: 银牙毫不犹豫地选了左边那条____的路，老舵认为有人提前给他通风报信。
particular:1.hook: Old Helm's gaze moved slowly to each face in our little group.
particular:1.line: 'That *particular* path was chosen too fast — someone gave him the answer,' Old Helm said.

consequence:1.en: Silverfang spread a map across the market table and grinned at Old Helm. 'One race around the outer ring,' he said. 'Winner takes the word.' Old Helm studied the route carefully. He knew that losing this bet carried a serious *consequence*: the troupe's only compass would be forfeit.
consequence:1.cnHint: 竞争船长在集市上提出赌约，老舵明白输掉的____可不小。
consequence:1.hook: Old Helm's hand hovered over the map, still undecided.
consequence:1.line: 'Losing has a *consequence* you may not be ready for, old friend.'

realize:1.en: I was carrying the supply crates through the island's morning market when I heard Silverfang laughing behind me. Suddenly I turned and saw our word fragment in his hand. Then I began to *realize* what was happening: he had not found it by chance — he had been following us all along.
realize:1.cnHint: 我在早市搬货时，渐渐____银牙一直在跟踪我们。
realize:1.hook: The word fragment glinted in Silverfang's fingers like a dare.
realize:1.line: 'You finally *realize* I have been two steps behind you all morning.'

mostly:1.en: The floating market opened at dawn. Stalls lined the wooden walkway above the clouds, selling maps, lanterns, and hot soup. The traders were *mostly* quiet, watching the sky for wind changes. Bell moved among them with a small notebook, asking careful questions about the route ahead.
mostly:1.cnHint: 小铃在集市上打听前方航路，摊贩们____沉默地观察着天空。
mostly:1.hook: One trader's answer made Bell stop writing entirely.
mostly:1.line: 'The pilots here are *mostly* honest — but watch the one in the red coat.'

exactly:1.en: Silverfang pointed to a spot on the canal bridge and told Old Helm to stand there. 'Wait,' said Old Helm. He studied the bridge, then the sky, then the bridge again. 'That is *exactly* the position where the wind funnel hits at noon. You want to slow us down.'
exactly:1.cnHint: 银牙指定老舵站在桥上某处，老舵意识到那____是正午强风汇聚的地方。
exactly:1.hook: Silverfang's smile did not deny a single word.
exactly:1.line: 'You placed us *exactly* where the wind would cost us the most time.'

vary:1.en: Bell explained the race route to the troupe near the canal steps. 'The wind currents *vary* from street to street here,' she said, tracing her finger along the map. 'A path that looks short may take three times as long if you fight the wrong current.' Everyone listened closely.
vary:1.cnHint: 小铃在运河台阶旁解释，这里各街道的气流会____，走错方向可能浪费大量时间。
vary:1.hook: Silverfang's crew had already chosen a different street.
vary:1.line: 'The currents *vary* — choose your lane before the bell sounds.'

brain:1.en: The puzzle lock on the word chest had twelve turning rings and no numbers. Silverfang had been trying for an hour and was ready to kick it. Old Helm knelt beside it, said nothing for a moment, then opened it in four moves. 'Age,' he said, 'feeds the *brain* well.'
brain:1.cnHint: 银牙对宝箱的谜题锁束手无策，老舵用____轻松解开了它。
brain:1.hook: Inside the chest lay something none of them had expected.
brain:1.line: 'A good *brain* beats a fast hand every single time.'

stress:1.en: The race was one hour away and our rope rigging had snapped. Bell worked fast, her face tight with *stress*. Around her, market crowds pushed and shouted. She tied the last knot just as Silverfang's crew sailed past, laughing. She looked up and said, calmly, 'We are ready.'
stress:1.cnHint: 比赛前绳索断裂，小铃在____中飞速修好了它。
stress:1.hook: Silverfang had not expected them to be ready at all.
stress:1.line: 'The *stress* only sharpens me — do not count us out yet.'

financial:1.en: Silverfang leaned on the dock rail and offered Old Helm a deal. 'I cover your port fees,' he said, 'and you hand me the word fragment after the race — win or lose.' Old Helm shook his head. He never accepted *financial* help from someone whose smile hid more than it showed.
financial:1.cnHint: 银牙向老舵提出用____援助换取词语碎片，老舵拒绝了这个笑里藏刀的提议。
financial:1.hook: Silverfang's offer was already waiting on a signed paper.
financial:1.line: 'A *financial* gift from me always comes with a price attached.'

fruit:1.en: The market island smelled of morning dew and ripe colour. Rows of stalls carried every kind of *fruit* — round, star-shaped, some I had no name for. Old Helm picked up a small golden one and smiled. 'Each island grows something different,' he said. 'That is the whole point of travelling.'
fruit:1.cnHint: 老舵在集市上拿起一颗金色的____，说旅行的意义就在于此。
fruit:1.hook: But one vendor's stall held something that was never meant to be eaten.
fruit:1.line: Old Helm: 'Every *fruit* here grew under a different sky — taste it slowly.'

waste:1.en: Silverfang leaned against his ship's rail, watching our troupe sort through a pile of old map scraps. 'You *waste* good wind standing still,' he called down, arms folded. Old Helm didn't look up. He laid one scrap flat and said, quietly, 'Speed without direction is the real waste.'
waste:1.cnHint: 银牙嘲笑我们在码头____时间，老舵低头整理地图碎片，不慌不忙。
waste:1.hook: Then Silverfang saw which scrap Old Helm had just placed on top.
waste:1.line: Silverfang: 'Don't *waste* your morning on scraps even seagulls ignore.'

learning:1.en: Bell spread a sky-chart across the dock and called the whole troupe over. She pointed to tiny symbols none of us recognised. 'Island navigation is a living *learning*,' she said, tracing a line with one finger. 'The sky rewrites the lesson every night, so you must keep reading it.'
learning:1.cnHint: 领航员在码头展开星图，说岛屿航行是一门活的____，夜夜都在改写。
learning:1.hook: One symbol on the chart, she admitted, she still could not read.
learning:1.line: Bell: 'True *learning* never sits still — the sky proves that every night.'

manager:1.en: At the trade post on Copper Ledge, a short woman in a bright-orange coat stopped us at the gate. She was the island's *manager*, responsible for every ship that docked and every word-fragment that changed hands. Old Helm bowed politely. She studied him without blinking, then opened the gate just wide enough for one person.
manager:1.cnHint: 在铜崖贸易站，岛屿____拦住了我们，只肯让一个人进去。
manager:1.hook: She looked past Old Helm and pointed — directly at me.
manager:1.line: Manager: 'I am the *manager* here, and I decide who carries words off this island.'

knowledge:1.en: Silverfang challenged Old Helm to name every island on the eastern rim from memory. Old Helm closed his eyes and listed them without pause. Silverfang's smile faded. 'That is an unfair amount of *knowledge* for one old man,' he muttered. Old Helm opened one eye. 'I earned it the same way you could — slowly.'
knowledge:1.cnHint: 银牙要求老舵背出东部所有岛屿名称，没想到对方的____让他哑口无言。
knowledge:1.hook: Silverfang then pulled out a map that Old Helm had never seen before.
knowledge:1.line: Old Helm: 'Every piece of *knowledge* I have was once a question I refused to drop.'

mental:1.en: The fog on Pale Bridge Island was so thick that Bell guided us by sound alone, tapping a small bell at each turn. Old Helm said the real danger was not the fog but the *mental* weight it placed on a navigator — doubt crept in fast when you could not see three steps ahead. Bell just kept tapping, steady as a clock.
mental:1.cnHint: 白桥岛的浓雾让人____压力巨大，但领航员始终平稳地敲着引路铃。
mental:1.hook: Then the tapping stopped, and we heard something tapping back.
mental:1.line: Bell: 'Keep your *mental* footing — fog lies, but your feet know the path.'

weight:1.en: Old Helm handed me a small chest before we crossed the rope bridge to Anvil Isle. 'Carry this,' he said simply. By the halfway point my arms shook. The *weight* was not iron or stone — it was a chest full of word-fragments, each one a place we had promised to find. I did not put it down.
weight:1.cnHint: 老舵让我扛一个装满地图碎片的小箱过桥，那____压得我双臂发抖，却让我不愿放手。
weight:1.hook: From the far end, Silverfang watched and said nothing — which was worse than any taunt.
weight:1.line: Old Helm: 'Feel the *weight* — that is how many places are still waiting for us.'

academic:1.en: A young scholar from the Lens Tower stopped our troupe on the stone path and asked to examine our word-fragments for his *academic* records. Bell politely unrolled one small piece. The scholar's eyes went wide. Old Helm smiled and said, 'Some knowledge lives in the air long before it reaches any tower.'
academic:1.cnHint: 镜塔来的学者拦下我们，想把地图碎片收入他的____档案，老舵含笑婉拒。
academic:1.hook: The scholar whispered that his tower had been searching for that fragment for thirty years.
academic:1.line: Bell: 'Our journey is the best *academic* work any of us will ever do.'

major:1.en: The floating market of Driftstone was loud and full of colour. Old Helm spread a worn map across a barrel and tapped a golden circle near the edge. 'This is a *major* crossing point,' he said. 'Every trade route on three islands meets right here.' Bell whistled softly. I understood then why we had come so far.
major:1.cnHint: 老舵在漂浮集市上指着地图说，这里是一个____的交汇点。
major:1.hook: Something beneath the barrel began to glow.
major:1.line: 'This is a *major* crossing point — every route on three islands meets here.'

communication:1.en: Silverfang docked her ship on the east pier and crossed her arms. 'Your troupe never sends word ahead,' she said. Old Helm shrugged. 'We prefer surprise.' Bell leaned over to me and whispered, 'Good *communication* between crews can save a whole voyage.' I filed that away as advice worth keeping.
communication:1.cnHint: 小铃悄悄告诉我，船员之间良好的____能拯救整段航程。
communication:1.hook: Silverfang's next words were not a whisper at all.
communication:1.line: 'Good *communication* between crews can save a whole voyage, you know.'

market:1.en: The island's *market* stretched from the stone arch all the way to the cloud-rail. Stalls sold bottled starlight, pressed sky-flowers, and maps drawn on moth wings. Old Helm moved through the crowd without touching a single jar. I knocked over two. Bell caught them both before they fell.
market:1.cnHint: 岛上的____从石拱门一直延伸到云轨，摆满了奇异的货物。
market:1.hook: One moth-wing map showed our next island — already circled in red.
market:1.line: 'This *market* hides the best map fragments on any island I have visited.'

apply:1.en: Bell knelt beside the old anchor-stone and opened a small tin. 'Watch,' she said, and began to *apply* a thin silver paste along the carved letters. Slowly the letters lit up one by one, spelling a word none of us had collected yet. Old Helm nodded. 'That is how you read a sleeping sign.'
apply:1.cnHint: 小铃在锚石的刻字上____了一种银色膏体，字母逐渐发光显现。
apply:1.hook: The last letter flickered, then went dark again.
apply:1.line: 'You have to *apply* the paste slowly, or the letters will not hold their light.'

per:1.en: Silverfang leaned against her ship's rail and quoted her price without blinking. 'Two sky-coins *per* word fragment, paid before you leave the pier.' Old Helm counted his coat pockets twice. I counted mine once and found only a button. Bell quietly placed four coins on the rail and smiled.
per:1.cnHint: 竞争船长开价，每个词碎片收取两枚空天币，要求在离开前付清。
per:1.hook: Silverfang pocketed the coins and handed over something unexpected instead.
per:1.line: 'Two sky-coins *per* fragment — that is the rate, and I do not haggle.'

treat:1.en: After the long climb up Driftstone's outer stair, Old Helm stopped at a small cart and bought three warm rolls filled with spiced cloud-fruit. He handed one to Bell, one to me, and kept the last. 'A hot meal is the best *treat* after a hard walk,' he said. He was absolutely right.
treat:1.cnHint: 爬完长梯后，老舵长买了热面包，说热乎的食物是辛苦跋涉后最好的____。
treat:1.hook: Bell's roll had a folded note tucked inside.
treat:1.line: 'A hot meal is the best *treat* after a climb like that, trust me.'

creative:1.en: The word-seller at the corner stall was a small woman with ink-stained fingers. She did not list her fragments by price. Instead she set a puzzle: solve it, take the word. Old Helm called her method *creative*. I called it exhausting. Bell solved it in four moves and pocketed the fragment, grinning.
creative:1.cnHint: 角落摊位的售词人用解谜来代替定价，老舵长称赞这个方法很____。
creative:1.hook: The puzzle reset itself and pointed at me next.
creative:1.line: 'That is a very *creative* way to run a stall — I have never seen it done before.'

perform:1.en: A small stage near the cloud-rail held three musicians who needed a fourth. Silverfang, passing by, paused. 'I can *perform* with you,' she said, picking up a spare string-bow. She played three clean notes and the whole market went quiet. I had no idea she could do that. Neither, it seemed, did she.
perform:1.cnHint: 银牙路过一个小舞台，主动加入表演，她的____让整个集市安静下来。
perform:1.hook: The last note unlocked a door none of us had noticed before.
perform:1.line: 'I can *perform* with your group — hand me that string-bow and I will show you.'

trouble:1.en: On the market deck of Windhollow Island, a merchant's crates had toppled and spilled coloured powder across the planks. Old Helm knelt down, brushing the mess aside. 'Every port brings its own *trouble*,' he said quietly, 'but every mess also hides something worth finding.' He lifted a crate — and beneath it lay a folded map.
trouble:1.cnHint: 老船长在市集甲板上翻开倒塌的箱子，发现了藏在____之下的地图。
trouble:1.hook: The map showed a place none of us had ever heard of.
trouble:1.line: 'Every port brings its own *trouble*, but every mess hides something worth finding.'

reflect:1.en: Bell stood at the edge of the sky-bridge, watching the twin moons *reflect* off the mist below. She had been quiet all morning. 'The light shows us what the dark hides,' she said at last, pointing down. A shape — large, slow, unmistakable — was rising through the silver glow.
reflect:1.cnHint: 领航员在天桥边凝视雾中的倒影，发现有什么东西正从____中升起。
reflect:1.hook: Whatever rose from the mist, it was heading straight for us.
reflect:1.line: 'Look — the moons *reflect* something moving far below us.'

attend:1.en: A notice board on the Crosswind Plaza read: ALL CREW MUST *ATTEND* THE CAPTAIN'S BRIEFING AT DAWN. Old Helm folded his arms. Silverfang had posted it. She had no right to call our crew anywhere. Yet her briefings, everyone admitted, had never once been a waste of time.
attend:1.cnHint: 银牙在广场张贴告示，要求所有船员____她黎明前的简报会。
attend:1.hook: Old Helm read it twice, then began walking toward the meeting point.
attend:1.line: 'All crew must *attend* — yes, even yours, Old Helm.'

belief:1.en: Silverfang leaned against the harbour post, arms crossed, watching our troupe unload supplies. 'Your *belief* that friendship beats a contract is sweet,' she said, tossing a coin in the air. 'But out past the Redwind Gap, sweet gets you nowhere.' She caught the coin and smiled — not unkindly.
belief:1.cnHint: 银牙在港口挑战老船长，质疑他对____的坚持是否经得起考验。
belief:1.hook: The coin she tossed landed showing a map — a real one.
belief:1.line: 'Your *belief* in friendship is sweet, but the Redwind Gap is not.'

carry:1.en: The morning trade bell rang across Ashpetal Wharf. Each member of our troupe had to *carry* a crate of wind-stones to the exchange booth before the bell rang again. Bell ran. I ran. Old Helm walked — and somehow arrived first, stones unspilt, humming a quiet tune.
carry:1.cnHint: 清晨，我们的队伍要在钟声结束前____风石箱到交易亭，老船长的方式出乎意料。
carry:1.hook: Old Helm set his crate down and said only, 'Pace wins.'
carry:1.line: '*Carry* it steady — hurry breaks more than it saves.'

else:1.en: After the others had chosen their sky-routes on the planning board, I stood there staring. Every path was marked: the safe ones, the fast ones, the scenic ones. Bell appeared beside me. 'Everyone *else* picks with their head,' she said softly, pressing a small compass into my palm. 'You pick with yours.'
else:1.cnHint: 规划路线时，其他人都做出了选择，领航员告诉我不必和____一样。
else:1.hook: The compass needle spun once and stopped, pointing somewhere new.
else:1.line: 'Everyone *else* has chosen — now it is your turn to decide.'

prepare:1.en: The market square of Windhollow Island buzzed with colour. Silverfang's crew had arrived before us, and we could see them *preparing* their stall — laying out charts, polishing brass tools, stacking bright signal flags. Old Helm watched with calm eyes. 'They move fast,' Bell whispered. 'Then we move smarter,' he replied.
prepare:1.cnHint: 在风谷岛的集市广场，我们看到银牙的船员正在____他们的摊位，老舵手示意我们保持冷静。
prepare:1.hook: Whatever Silverfang was selling, every island captain wanted one.
prepare:1.line: 'We *prepare* our table before they open their mouths,' Old Helm said.

workplace:1.en: Silverfang led us through the deck workshops of Ironhook Station, where crafters shaped map-glass under open sky. 'This is my *workplace*,' she said proudly, arms wide. Sparks drifted like tiny stars. Old Helm ran a finger along a finished chart and nodded slowly. Bell scribbled notes without looking up.
workplace:1.cnHint: 银牙带我们参观了铁钩站的甲板工坊，她自豪地称这里是她的____。
workplace:1.hook: One unfinished chart on the far bench carried a name none of us recognised.
workplace:1.line: 'Every corner of this *workplace* holds a secret,' Silverfang said softly.

post:1.en: At the base of the great Wind-Needle pillar, travellers gathered to read notices. Silverfang had *posted* a bold challenge on the board: any troupe who could name three lost islands before sundown would win her finest chart. Old Helm read it twice. Bell grinned. I felt my pulse quicken.
post:1.cnHint: 银牙在风针柱的公告栏上____了一份大胆挑战书，老舵手仔细读了两遍。
post:1.hook: Sundown was less than two hours away.
post:1.line: 'I *post* this challenge for every troupe brave enough to answer,' Silverfang called out.

complete:1.en: Silverfang spread the puzzle-chart across the stone table: a ring of islands with three pieces missing. 'Find the gaps,' she said. Old Helm studied it quietly, then placed one tile, then another, then a third. The map glowed faintly. '*Complete*,' he murmured. Silverfang's eyes went wide with surprise.
complete:1.cnHint: 银牙摆出一张残缺的拼图海图，老舵手一一填补空缺，将其____。
complete:1.hook: The glow faded — and revealed a path none of us had ever seen.
complete:1.line: 'At last the map is *complete*,' Old Helm said quietly.

measure:1.en: Bell stood at the edge of Drift Pier and stretched a long cord across the gap between two floating platforms. She *measured* the distance three times, muttering numbers. Silverfang leaned on a post nearby, watching with thin amusement. 'Trusting your rope more than your eyes?' she asked. Bell just smiled.
measure:1.cnHint: 贝尔在漂流码头边用绳子反复____两个浮台之间的距离，银牙在旁边冷眼旁观。
measure:1.hook: The gap was wider than any rope we carried.
measure:1.line: 'I always *measure* twice before I trust a bridge,' Bell said firmly.

recommend:1.en: Outside the spice-stalls of Amber Arch, a friendly trader offered us three routes forward. Old Helm listened carefully, then turned to the trader. 'Which path do you *recommend* for a troupe carrying glass charts?' The trader paused, looked at our bags, and pointed without hesitation toward the high cloud road.
recommend:1.cnHint: 在琥珀拱廊的香料摊外，老舵手向一位商人询问哪条路线值得____。
recommend:1.hook: The cloud road had been closed for a season — until this morning.
recommend:1.line: 'I *recommend* the high road; the others have been restless lately,' the trader said.

resource:1.en: Silverfang laid her cards on the table at Coppergate Crossing. 'Your troupe has heart,' she admitted, 'but heart is not a *resource* that fuels a ship.' Old Helm reached into his coat and set down three glowing word-shards. The light caught Silverfang's face. She was quiet for a long moment.
resource:1.cnHint: 在铜门路口，银牙说热情不是什么____，老舵手随即拿出三块发光的文字碎片回应她。
resource:1.hook: Silverfang had never seen word-shards glow that colour before.
resource:1.line: 'Courage is a fine *resource*, but charts keep you alive,' Silverfang said coolly.

specific:1.en: Before the bet was sealed, Bell raised her hand. 'We need *specific* terms,' she said clearly, setting a small notebook on the barrel between us and Silverfang. 'Which islands count? Which charts are the prize?' Silverfang blinked, then laughed — a real laugh. 'Your navigator is sharper than you look,' she told Old Helm.
specific:1.cnHint: 在赌约正式定下之前，贝尔要求列出____的条款，让银牙刮目相看。
specific:1.hook: Silverfang picked up the pen and began to write something unexpected.
specific:1.line: 'Give me *specific* terms or the deal means nothing,' Bell said calmly.

positive:2.en: Bell spread a crinkled chart across the deck. Strange ink marks covered every corner. 'These aren't random,' she said quietly. Old Helm leaned in. The markings were *positive* signs — each one pointing toward the next island, like a trail of hopeful arrows left by someone who wanted us to follow.
positive:2.cnHint: 小铃在甲板上展开一张布满标记的旧图，发现这些符号都是____的指引。
positive:2.hook: But who had drawn them, and were they still watching?
positive:2.line: 'Every *positive* mark on this chart is a step someone took before us.'

economic:2.en: We drifted into a small harbour island where merchants packed stalls along the edge of the cloud. Old Helm picked up a tiny ledger left on a crate. Its pages tracked the *economic* flow of the whole sky-route — which islands traded, which ones starved, which ones had simply vanished from the record.
economic:2.cnHint: 老舵主在市集中发现一本记录天空航线____往来的账本。
economic:2.hook: The last entry was dated the morning Silverfang first appeared.
economic:2.line: 'This *economic* record tells us more than any map ever could.'

link:2.en: Inside an old lighthouse on the edge of Amber Isle, Bell found a chain hanging from the ceiling. One ring was missing. She held it up and said the absent ring was the *link* between two halves of a hidden route — without it, the path split and led travelers in circles forever.
link:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔里发现一条断裂的链，那枚缺失的____牵连着一条隐秘的航路。
link:2.hook: Silverfang's ship had been circling this island for three days.
link:2.line: 'Find the missing *link* and the whole route opens up to us.'

produce:2.en: Old Helm handed me a small brass box found wedged beneath the helm. When I turned its key, the box began to *produce* a soft, rising hum that grew into a clear musical note. Bell pressed her ear close and whispered that the note matched the frequency the old star-charts used to mark safe passage.
produce:2.cnHint: 老舵主找到一只铜盒，转动钥匙后它____出一个与古老星图频率吻合的音符。
produce:2.hook: The hum grew louder the closer we steered toward the storm.
produce:2.line: 'It will *produce* the exact tone only when we are on the right path.'

teach:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked wall on the Isle of Echoes, I found a short letter in a careful hand. A traveller had once paused here to *teach* a child the names of the star-roads, writing each one down so the lesson would last longer than memory. The final name on the list was one Old Helm had never heard.
teach:2.cnHint: 在回声岛的石缝里，我发现一封旅人留下的信，他曾在此____孩子认识星路的名字。
teach:2.hook: That last star-road name matched the symbol on Silverfang's flag.
teach:2.line: 'Someone chose to *teach* a child the very secret we are chasing.'

worth:2.en: Silverfang left a sealed pouch on our deck before dawn — no note, just a single glowing stone inside. Old Helm turned it over slowly. He said the stone was *worth* nothing as a gem, but as a key to the Tide Gate it was everything. His voice was steady, but his hands were not.
worth:2.cnHint: 竞争船长在甲板上留下一枚石头，老舵主说它作为宝石毫无价值，但作为潮汐门的钥匙____得上一切。
worth:2.hook: Accepting it meant accepting whatever deal came with it.
worth:2.line: 'It is *worth* more as a key than as anything else in the sky.'

common:2.en: Bell lined up three maps from three different captains on the cabin table. At first glance they showed entirely different skies. But one feature appeared on every single one — a small blank circle drawn in the same corner. That blank was their only *common* mark, and it sat exactly where our compass refused to point.
common:2.cnHint: 小铃对比三位船长的航图，发现它们唯一____的标记是同一个空白圆圈。
common:2.hook: No captain had ever written a single word inside that circle.
common:2.line: 'The only *common* mark on all three maps is the one no one will explain.'
